In the ancient Church the newly baptised came up from the water and were dressed in white; in our own baptismal rite the child is clothed in a white garment as a sign of the new self. Paul's last line sets the boundaries of that new family very wide: “In that renewal there is no longer Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave and free; but Christ is all and in all!” Every division that human beings use to rank one another, nation, culture, class or caste, has no place in the family born from the font. Whoever kneels at the same altar and receives the same Body has the same Father. To put on the new self is to see every baptised person as a brother or sister clothed in the same Christ.
outline: Opening
Nicodemus by night: can one who has grown old start again?
Point 1 · Born from above
Water and Spirit, and the font as the womb of the Church.
Point 2 · The wind blows where it chooses
The slow journey of Nicodemus from night into day.
Point 3 · Put on the new self
What must die, what we wear, and a family without walls.
Take-home line
“You must be born from above.”
live: Remember your Baptism (John 3:5)
Find out the date of your Baptism and the church where you were baptised; on that date each year, thank God and renew your baptismal promises.
Take off one old garment (Colossians 3:8–9)
Choose one sin of the mouth, anger, slander, abusive words or lying, and fight it deliberately for the rest of this Easter season.
fathers: St Ambrose of Milan (in substance)

To the newly baptised he said: you went down into the water, and then you came up. Then you received white garments, as a sign that you had put off the covering of sin and put on the chaste robe of innocence. The Church, clothed in these garments, says with the Song of Songs: I am black and beautiful; black through the frailty of my human condition, beautiful through grace.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)

In his hymns he says that the robe of glory Adam lost in Paradise is given back in the water of Baptism. Christ went down into the Jordan and left the robe there for us; whoever goes down into the font comes up clothed in the light that Adam had forfeited.
magis: Catechism 1215

Baptism is called the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit, for it signifies and actually brings about the birth of water and the Spirit without which no one can enter the kingdom of God.
Catechism 1243
The white garment symbolises that the person baptised has put on Christ and has risen with Christ; the candle, lit from the Easter candle, signifies that Christ has enlightened the neophyte.
Catechism 1934–1935

All persons, created in the image of the one God and redeemed by the one Christ, enjoy an equal dignity; every form of social or cultural discrimination is to be curbed and eradicated as incompatible with God's design.
2027-04-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you received Nicodemus by night and told him that he must be born from above. We thank you for the new birth we received from water and the Spirit in the font of the Church. Put to death in us whatever is earthly, take away anger, slander and lies from our mouths, and clothe us again and again with the new self, renewed in the image of our Creator. Make every baptised person a brother and sister to us, for you are all and in all. Amen. Alleluia!
altar: Those born of water and the Spirit are led to the altar: Baptism opens the door, and the Holy Qurbana nourishes the life it began. The same Christ who clothes us in the font feeds us at the one table, where no one ranks above another and “Christ is all and in all!”

2027-04-29.title: Fifth Thursday of Resurrection · St Catherine of Siena
2027-04-29.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Do not turn away from the living God
The giver of life to all
2027-04-29.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. St Catherine of Siena, virgin and doctor of the Church: 1 John 1:5–2:2; Matthew 11:25–30.
2027-04-29.verse: Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
theo: The Letter to the Hebrews takes up a psalm that the Church still prays at the opening of her daily prayer, Psalm 95, and hears in it the voice of the Holy Spirit speaking now: “Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says, ‘Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, as on the day of testing in the wilderness.’” The generation that came out of Egypt had seen the sea divided, eaten manna and drunk from the rock, and still their hearts grew hard. Seeing great works of God does not by itself make a heart soft. The writer then speaks to his own community with deep concern: “Take care, brothers and sisters, that none of you may have an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God. But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called ‘today,’ so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.” Two things stand out. First, the word ‘today’. God never speaks to us about tomorrow; his invitation is always for this day. Second, we are responsible for one another. A hard heart rarely forms in a moment; it hardens slowly, by small refusals, and the remedy is daily encouragement within the Christian family. A word from a friend, a parent or a priest at the right time can keep a heart from setting like cement.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks with the authority of the Son to whom the Father has given life: “Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.” The tense matters: has eternal life, has passed. Eternal life begins now, in the one who believes. Then Jesus speaks of two moments. The first is already here: “the hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.” Those who are dead in sin hear his voice and rise by faith. The second is still to come: “for the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear his voice and will come out”, those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of condemnation. The Church professes this in every Creed: the resurrection of the body. In our parishes, families go to the cemetery after the Holy Qurbana on many feasts and anniversaries, light candles and pray at the graves of their dead. In the season of the Resurrection those graves look different. They are not the end of a story but a waiting room. The One who called Lazarus out of the tomb will one day speak to every grave, and the bodies laid there in faith will hear his voice.

Today the Church remembers St Catherine of Siena, and the readings given for her fit the whole day. Born in Siena in 1347, one of the youngest of the many children of a wool dyer, she gave herself to Christ as a girl and joined the Dominican laywomen known as the Mantellate. She had little schooling and learned to read late, yet she became one of the great teachers of the Church: her book of the Dialogue and nearly four hundred letters were dictated to her companions. Her first reading proclaims that “God is light and in him there is no darkness at all”, and that “If we confess our sins, he who is faithful and just will forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” Catherine knew her own sinfulness and spent herself bringing others to confession and reconciliation. Her Gospel is Jesus' prayer: “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants.” This unlettered young woman wrote with burning frankness to princes, cardinals and the Pope himself. She urged Pope Gregory XI to return from Avignon to Rome, and he did so in 1377; she worked for peace between warring cities and for the unity of the Church when the great schism began. Worn out, she died in Rome on 29 April 1380, aged thirty-three. St Paul VI declared her a doctor of the Church in 1970, and St John Paul II named her a patron of Europe in 1999. Catherine lived the ‘today’ of Hebrews: she never put off what love asked of her. Her life tells every Christian, especially women and lay people, that holiness and the word of truth are not reserved for the learned.
outline: Opening
‘Today’: God never speaks to us about tomorrow.
Point 1 · Do not harden your hearts
The wilderness generation, and exhorting one another every day.
Point 2 · From death to life
Eternal life now, and the voice that will open every grave.
Point 3 · Revealed to infants
St Catherine of Siena: light, confession and fearless love.
Take-home line
“Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
live: Exhort one another today (Hebrews 3:13)
Send one message of encouragement in faith today to someone who is struggling or drifting from the Church.
Pray at a grave (John 5:28)
Visit the grave of a family member this week, or pray for them at home, professing: I believe in the resurrection of the body.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)

There are two resurrections. The first happens now, when souls dead in sin hear the voice of the Son of God and rise by faith; the second will come at the end, when bodies hear his voice and come out of the tombs. Whoever does not wish to be condemned in the second resurrection, let him rise in the first.
St Catherine of Siena (in substance)

Eternal Trinity, you are a deep sea: the more I enter you, the more I find, and the more I find, the more I seek you. And to her disciples she wrote: if you are what you ought to be, you will set the whole world on fire.
magis: Catechism 998
All the dead will rise: those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgement.
Catechism 1847
God created us without us, but he did not will to save us without us; to receive his mercy we must admit our faults: if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us.
Catechism 313
Quoting St Catherine of Siena: everything comes from love, all is ordained for the salvation of man; God does nothing without this goal in mind.
saints: Today
St Catherine of Siena (1347–1380), virgin, Dominican laywoman, mystic and doctor of the Church; patron of Italy and of Europe.
2027-04-29.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the Father, you have life in yourself and you give it to all who hear your word. Today, as we hear your voice, do not let our hearts be hardened. Raise us now from the death of sin, and on the last day call us out of our graves to the resurrection of life. Through the prayers of St Catherine of Siena, give us her light, her humility to confess our sins, her courage to speak the truth in love, and her fire for the unity of your Church. Amen. Alleluia!
altar: The Holy Qurbana is the pledge of the resurrection: whoever eats the Body of the Risen Lord has eternal life now, and he will raise them up on the last day. St Catherine received this Bread with burning love; her companions tell that in her last years, when she could take hardly any food, it was her strength.

2027-04-30.title: Fifth Friday of Resurrection
2027-04-30.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-04-30.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. Tomorrow the month of May begins, kept in many Syro-Malabar homes and parishes as the month of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2027-04-30.verse: For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
theo: Paul arrived in Corinth after a hard experience in Athens, where his learned speech on the Areopagus had won only a few believers (Acts 17:32–34). Corinth was a rich port city that loved clever talk and public speakers. Paul decided to do the opposite of what would impress it. “When I came to you, brothers and sisters, I did not come proclaiming the mystery of God to you in lofty words or wisdom. For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.” He does not hide his own condition: “And I came to you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling.” Yet the Church of Corinth was born from that trembling preacher, because something other than eloquence was at work: “My speech and my proclamation were not with plausible words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit and of power, so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God.” We read this in the season of the Resurrection, and it reminds us that the Risen Lord is the Crucified Lord. He showed Thomas his hands and his side (John 20:27); his wounds were not erased by Easter but glorified. That is why a Syro-Malabar Christian keeps Friday as the day of the Cross even in the weeks of Easter joy, and why the crucifix and the empty tomb are never separated in our faith.

In the Gospel Jesus calls the crowd and says: “Listen and understand: it is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but it is what comes out of the mouth that defiles.” The context is a question about washing hands before meals according to the tradition of the elders. The care of the Pharisees for purity was sincere, and the debate is one within the family of Israel, among teachers who all loved the Law; the Church reads it without any contempt for the Jewish people, from whom Jesus, his mother and the apostles came. Jesus moves the question from the hands to the heart. When Peter asks for an explanation, he says: “But what comes out of the mouth proceeds from the heart, and this is what defiles. For out of the heart come evil intentions, murder, adultery, fornication, theft, false witness, slander. These are what defile a person, but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile.” Notice where the list begins: with evil intentions, the thoughts no one else sees. And notice where it ends: false witness and slander, sins of the tongue. Between the hidden thought and the spoken word lies the whole of our moral life. Outward observance matters, and the Church keeps her fasts and her rites with love; but Jesus will not let any rite take the place of a clean heart.

Today a great deal of what ‘comes out of the mouth’ comes out through the fingers. A message forwarded without checking, a rumour about a neighbour's daughter passed on in a family group, a mocking comment under a priest's photograph: Jesus' list has not gone out of date. False witness and slander now travel in seconds to hundreds of people. The question Jesus asks is not first about our phones but about our hearts: what is inside, that comes out so easily? Paul's answer is the Crucified. A heart that has decided to know Christ crucified becomes slow to condemn, because it knows what it cost to forgive its own sins. Tomorrow the month of May begins, and in many of our homes the Marian month devotion will be prayed each evening. The Blessed Virgin Mary is the model of the clean heart: of her the Gospel says twice that she treasured the words and events of her Son and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19, 51). What came out of her mouth was the Magnificat. Let us ask our Mother to teach us, through this month, to keep our hearts clean, so that our words, spoken or typed, may build up and not destroy.
outline: Opening
A trembling preacher in a city that loved clever speech.
Point 1 · Jesus Christ, and him crucified
The power of God in weakness, and the Risen One who keeps his wounds.
Point 2 · Out of the heart
From the hands to the heart: what really defiles.
Point 3 · Words that come out through the fingers
Slander in the family group, and the clean heart of the Mother of God.
Take-home line
“I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.”
live: Check before you forward (Matthew 15:19)
Today, before forwarding any message about a person, ask: is it true, is it kind, is it necessary? If not, delete it.
Begin the Marian month
Prepare the prayer corner at home for the May devotion, and decide on a time each evening when the family will pray together.
fathers: Aphrahat the Persian Sage (in substance)

Purity of heart is prayer more than all the prayers that are said aloud, and silence joined to a sincere mind is better than a loud voice. Give me your heart, says God; when the heart is pure, the offering is accepted.
St John Chrysostom (in substance)

See the power of the Cross: fishermen and tentmakers, unlearned and poor, persuaded the whole world. If they had been eloquent and powerful, people would have said it was their skill; but because they were weak, it was clear that the victory belonged to the Crucified.
magis: Catechism 272

Faith in God the Father almighty can be put to the test by the experience of evil; but God revealed his almighty power in the voluntary humiliation and the Resurrection of his Son: Christ crucified is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
Catechism 1853
Sin has its root in the heart of man, in his free will; out of the heart come evil intentions, murder, adultery, theft, false witness, slander.
Catechism 2517–2519
The heart is the seat of the moral personality; the pure in heart, who have attuned their minds and wills to the demands of God's holiness, are promised that they will see God.
2027-04-30.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, crucified and risen, you kept the wounds of your Passion in your glory. Let us know nothing but you, and you crucified, so that our faith may rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God. Create in us a clean heart, take away the evil intentions from which our sins of word and deed are born, and guard our tongues and our fingers from false witness and slander. Through the prayers of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who kept your words in her heart, prepare us for the month dedicated to her. Amen. Alleluia!
altar: At every Holy Qurbana the Church proclaims Christ crucified and risen: the sacrifice of the Cross is made present, and the Lord gives us his Body and Blood. Before receiving him we pray for a clean heart, for it is not what goes into the mouth that defiles, but this Bread makes holy those who receive it worthily.

quick: Isaiah: nations that do not know you shall run to you; my word shall not return to me empty.
Acts: the believers were of one heart and soul, and there was not a needy person among them.
Jesus comes through locked doors, breathes the Spirit for the forgiveness of sins, and Thomas confesses: My Lord and my God!
2027-04-04.action: At the elevation of the Host and Chalice today, say in your heart: My Lord and my God.
2027-04-04.question: Do I bring my doubts to the Lord within the community, or do I walk away with them?
catechism: The doubt of the disciples and the real risen body.
kidsaint: St Thomas the Apostle (Mar Thoma)

Thomas was one of Jesus' twelve apostles. When the others said Jesus was alive, Thomas said he would not believe unless he touched Jesus' wounds. A week later Jesus came and said, ‘Touch my hands, Thomas, and believe.’ Thomas fell down and said: ‘My Lord and my God!’ Our tradition tells that Thomas later travelled all the way to Kerala to tell our ancestors about Jesus. Lesson: when you have questions, bring them to Jesus, and stay with his Church!
2027-04-04.special: Second Sunday of Resurrection: New Sunday (Puthu Njayar), the Sunday of the Neophytes, the confession of Mar Thoma.
term: Puthu Njayar (New Sunday)

The Kerala name for the Sunday after Easter, the eighth day of the Resurrection. It is called new because Christ makes all things new, and because the newly baptised began their new life among the faithful. For St Thomas Christians it is the day of Mar Thoma's confession, ‘My Lord and my God’, and the high point of the pilgrimage to Malayattoor.

family.explain: Thomas was not with the other disciples when Jesus came on Easter night. He said: “I will not believe unless I touch his wounds.” A week later Jesus came again and said: “Thomas, put your finger here. Do not doubt, believe!” Thomas said: “My Lord and my God!” Jesus said that people who believe without seeing him are blessed. That means us! We cannot see Jesus with our eyes, but he is really with us, especially in the Holy Qurbana.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always believe in Jesus, even when we cannot see him, and say with Mar Thoma: My Lord and my God.
family.ask: Ask: “When the priest lifts up the Host at Qurbana, what can we say quietly to Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A software engineer in Bengaluru had not been to the Holy Qurbana for six years. He called himself an honest doubter. When his grandmother died in Pala, he went home for the funeral and sat in the front pew beside her empty chair. As a boy he had always stood next to her at Qurbana, and at the elevation she would squeeze his hand and whisper, ‘Ente Karthave, ente Daivame.’ At her funeral Qurbana, when the priest lifted up the Host, he felt the old pressure of her hand that was no longer there, and before he could think, he heard himself whispering her words. He did not stop having questions. But the next Sunday he went to the Holy Qurbana in Bengaluru, and the Sunday after that. ‘Thomas had his questions too,’ he told the priest at confession some months later. ‘But he came back on the eighth day.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you come through locked doors and say, Peace be with you. Come into our gathering, show us your wounds, and breathe on us your Spirit. Amen. Alleluia!
share: The doors were locked for fear (John 20:19). What fears have locked the doors of my heart?
Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven (John 20:22–23). When did I last receive the Lord's forgiveness in confession?
Unless I see... I will not believe (John 20:25). What doubts do I carry, and do I bring them to the Lord in his Church?
They were of one heart and soul (Acts 4:32). Is there anyone in need among us whom I could help?
pm.resp: My Lord and my God, we believe in you.
interc: For the Syro-Malabar Church and all the St Thomas Christians, in Kerala and in every land of migration, that they may keep the faith of Mar Thoma.
For the newly baptised, who today take their place among the faithful, that they may persevere in their new life.
For those who doubt or have drifted away from the Church, that the Risen Lord may come to them on the eighth day.
For priests, ministers of the Lord's mercy in the Sacrament of Reconciliation.
For the poor and needy, that our parishes may be one heart and soul, with no one in need among us.
For the pilgrims of Malayattoor and of every shrine of Mar Thoma, that their climb may become a confession of faith.
pm.close: Father, on this new day you made your Son the firstborn from the dead and reconciled all things through the blood of his Cross. Breathe on us your Holy Spirit, forgive our sins, and make us blessed among those who have not seen and yet believe. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah: My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
Gamaliel: If this undertaking is of God, you will not be able to overthrow it.
Paul: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing.
Thomas asks the way; Jesus answers: I am the way, and the truth, and the life.
2027-04-11.action: Welcome one newcomer or lonely person at church today.
2027-04-11.question: Am I following Jesus as the Way, or looking for some other road?
catechism: Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.
kidsaint: St Thomas the Apostle

At the Last Supper Thomas asked Jesus, ‘Lord, we don't know where you are going. How can we know the way?’ Jesus answered, ‘I am the way!’ Later Thomas travelled all the way to India to tell people about Jesus. That is why we in Kerala are called Saint Thomas Christians! Lesson: it is good to ask Jesus questions, and Jesus himself is the way to God.
2027-04-11.special: Third Sunday of Resurrection. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Mar Addai and Mar Mari.
term: Rushma

A Syriac word meaning ‘sign’ or ‘mark’. In the Syro-Malabar Church it is the word for making the sign of the cross over persons and things in blessing, as the priest does over the people and over the holy gifts. It recalls the seal of the Holy Spirit with which the baptised are marked as belonging to Christ (Ephesians 1:13).

family.explain: Jesus told his friends: ‘Don't be worried. In my Father's house there are many rooms. I am going to get a place ready for you.’ Thomas said, ‘But we don't know the way!’ Jesus said, ‘I am the way.’ If we stay close to Jesus, he will lead us home to God the Father.
family.intention: We pray for all who feel lost, and for people who have come to our parish from far away.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we stay close to Jesus, our Way, this week?”

illus: An illustration

An old man from Angamaly climbed the hill of Malayattoor every year in the Easter season, as his father had done before him. The year he turned seventy-five he took his grandson, a boy of twelve, and they started before dawn. Halfway up, in the dark, the boy stopped and asked, ‘Appachan, how do you know the way? I can't see anything.’ The old man pointed ahead: ‘You see the people walking in front of us, and the small crosses beside the path? I don't need to see the top. I only need to follow.’ When they reached the summit as the sun came up, the old man knelt at the shrine and said quietly, ‘Thomas also did not know the way. The Lord told him, I am the way. That is enough for me.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, our Way, our Truth and our Life, gather us now in your Father's house of prayer, and calm our troubled hearts. Amen. Alleluia!
share: For my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples (Isaiah 56:7). Who feels like a stranger in my parish, and how can I welcome them?
If it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them (Acts 5:39). What fear about the Church or my family can I leave in God's hands?
He chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world (Ephesians 1:4). What does it mean to me that God chose me before I was born?
Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way? (John 14:5). What question would I like to ask Jesus today?
pm.resp: Lord Jesus, you are the way, the truth and the life.
interc: For the Syro-Malabar Church and all the Saint Thomas Christians, that we may walk faithfully in the way of our father in faith.
For migrants, refugees and all who feel like strangers, that they may find a home in the Church.
For the Jewish people, and in gratitude for teachers like Gamaliel, that God may bless them in his faithfulness.
For those who are troubled and afraid, that they may believe in God and in Christ.
For the Church in mission lands, that her works may be greater than our hopes.
pm.close: Blessed are you, Father, for every spiritual blessing given us in Christ. Through him, the Way, lead us to yourself; seal us with your Holy Spirit; and make your Church a house of prayer for all peoples. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah: a mother may forget her child, but God will never forget us; our names are on his palms.
Acts: the Spirit is given through the apostles; God's gift cannot be bought. Ephesians: by grace we have been made alive with Christ.
John: your pain will turn into joy, and no one will take your joy from you.
2027-04-18.action: Pray every day this week for one vocation to the priesthood or religious life from your own family or parish.
2027-04-18.question: Do I treat God's gifts as things to own or use, and do I believe that my sorrow can be turned into joy?
catechism: God's love stronger than a mother's.
The laying on of hands and the gift of the Spirit.
kidsaint: St Philip the Deacon

Philip was one of seven good men chosen by the apostles to serve the poor. He loved Jesus so much that he went to Samaria and told everyone about him. Many people were healed and there was great joy in that city! Later he explained the Bible to a traveller from Ethiopia and baptised him by the road. Philip had four daughters who also served God. Lesson: when we love Jesus, we want to share him with everyone, and our whole family can serve him!
2027-04-18.special: Fourth Sunday of the Resurrection. World Prayer Day for Vocations.
term: Simony

The buying or selling of spiritual things, such as sacraments, blessings or Church offices. The name comes from Simon the magician, who offered the apostles money for the power to give the Holy Spirit (Acts 8:18–20). The Church teaches that God's gifts are received freely and must be given freely.

family.explain: Before Jesus died, he told his friends: you will be sad for a little while, but then you will see me again, and your hearts will be full of joy. And that is what happened at Easter! Jesus also said that God never forgets us, just as a mother never forgets her baby. Today the whole Church prays that many boys and girls will hear God calling them to be priests and sisters.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and the sisters who serve us, and for young people whom God is calling.
family.ask: Ask: “What would we say if God called someone in our family to be a priest or a sister?”

illus: An illustration

A young woman from a parish near Kanjirappally, the only daughter of her parents, told them after her degree that she wanted to join a congregation of sisters. Her father refused to speak to her for three months. He had dreamed of her wedding, and he felt that God was taking away his only child. Her mother prayed quietly every evening, saying only, “Lord, you gave her to us; you will not forget us.” On the day of her first profession, the father came, sat at the back and wept through the whole Qurbana. Afterwards he said to the parish priest: “I thought I was losing a daughter. Today I saw that God has given her many children.” Years later, when she was working among migrant families in North India, he visited her every year, and the children there called him Appachan.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen and living, you have written our names on your hands. Turn our sorrow into joy as we gather, and send labourers into your harvest. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Can a woman forget her nursing child? (Isaiah 49:15). When have I felt forgotten by God, and how did he show me his love?
You thought you could obtain God's gift with money (Acts 8:20). Do I treat any holy thing as something to own or use?
But God, who is rich in mercy (Ephesians 2:4). From what death has God raised me?
Your pain will turn into joy (John 16:20). What sorrow do I need to give to the Lord today?
pm.resp: Lord of the harvest, send labourers.
interc: For our Holy Father, our Major Archbishop, our bishops and all priests, that they may serve with joy and give freely what they have freely received.
For young people whom God is calling to the priesthood and religious life, that they may hear his voice and answer generously.
For parents, that they may welcome the vocations of their children as a gift and not a loss.
For priests and religious who are tired, discouraged or lonely, that their sorrow may be turned into joy.
For all who feel forgotten by God, that they may know their names are written on his hands.
For our parish, that it may be a home where vocations are born and nourished.
pm.close: Father, rich in mercy, you made us alive with Christ and you never forget your people. Turn our sorrow into joy, and send into your harvest priests and religious after your own heart. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah: the despised Servant will be honoured by kings; the prisoners are called out; heaven and earth sing for joy.
Acts: Saul hears the Risen Lord: why do you persecute me? I am Jesus.
Hebrews: through the blood of Jesus, let us approach with a true heart and not neglect to meet together.
John: at daybreak the Lord fills the nets and says, Come and have breakfast.
2027-04-25.action: Invite one person who has stopped coming to bring them with you to the Sunday Qurbana.
2027-04-25.question: Do I recognise the Lord when he stands on the shore of my ordinary week?
catechism: The Risen Lord eats with his disciples.
kidsaint: Mar Addai

An old story says that King Abgar of Edessa was very sick and wanted to meet Jesus. After Jesus rose and went up to heaven, the apostle Thomas sent a disciple called Addai to the king. Addai prayed, the king was healed, and the whole city came to know Jesus. Our Holy Qurbana still uses a prayer named after Mar Addai and his helper Mar Mari. Lesson: when we pray the Qurbana, we pray with the first Christians!
2027-04-25.special: Fifth Sunday of Resurrection (Mar Addai). St Mark the Evangelist not kept this year.
term: Anaphora of Addai and Mari

The ancient Eucharistic prayer of the East Syriac tradition, named after the apostles of Edessa and Mesopotamia, and used in most Syro-Malabar Qurbanas. Scholars count it among the oldest Christian Eucharistic prayers; in 2001 the Holy See recognised its validity even in the form used by the Assyrian Church of the East, which has no explicit narrative of the Last Supper.

family.explain: Peter and his friends went fishing all night and caught nothing. In the morning a man on the beach told them to throw the net on the right side, and the net was filled with fish! John said, “It is the Lord!” Peter jumped into the water to reach Jesus first. Jesus had made a fire and cooked breakfast for them. He said, “Come and have breakfast.” Jesus still invites us to eat with him every Sunday at the Holy Qurbana.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and all who work hard and come home tired, and for families who cannot come to church together.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do to make Sunday a special day with Jesus in our family?”

illus: An illustration

A fisherman from Neendakara used to say that the hardest nights at sea were not the stormy ones but the empty ones: hours of work, and nothing in the net. One season after many such nights he told his wife he would skip the Sunday Qurbana to mend nets and go out again. She said nothing, but packed him a breakfast, and on the lid of the tiffin box she had written: ‘Come and have breakfast. John 21:12’. He laughed, then went to the Qurbana after all, and sat near the back. The Gospel that morning was the miraculous catch. He said later, “The fish came back that season. But what I remember is that Jesus cooked for fishermen who had caught nothing. I had thought he only wanted my catch. He wanted me.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you stood on the shore at daybreak and called your disciples to breakfast. Stand among us now; we know that it is you. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Sing for joy, O heavens, and exult, O earth (Isaiah 49:13). What has God done for me this Easter that makes me want to sing?
Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? (Acts 9:4). Where have I wounded Christ by wounding his people?
Not neglecting to meet together… but encouraging one another (Hebrews 10:25). Whom can I encourage to come back to the Sunday assembly?
Come and have breakfast (John 21:12). What does it mean to me that Jesus prepares the table?
pm.resp: It is the Lord! Alleluia!
interc: For our Church, heir of Mar Thoma and of Mar Addai and Mar Mari, that she may treasure her apostolic faith and liturgy.
For Christians in the lands of the ancient Church of the East, in Iraq, Syria and Iran, that they may be strengthened and live in peace.
For persecutors of Christians, that the Risen Lord may meet them as he met Saul.
For those who have stopped coming to the Sunday Qurbana, that they may hear the Lord's invitation again.
For fishermen and all who labour, that their work may be blessed and their nets filled.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son and made him known to his disciples at the breaking of bread. Through the prayers of Mar Addai and Mar Mari, keep us faithful to the faith of the apostles, gather us every Sunday at your table, and send us out as fishers of people. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah: sing, O barren one; enlarge your tent; my steadfast love shall not depart from you.
Acts: seven men full of the Spirit are chosen to serve the neglected widows, and the word of God spreads.
Jesus sends the Twelve: you received without payment; give without payment.
2027-04-01.action: Visit or call one widow or widower today who may feel forgotten.
2027-04-01.question: What have I received freely from God, and what am I giving freely in return?
kidsaint: St Philip the Deacon

Philip was one of the seven men chosen to help the apostles care for the poor. Later he went to Samaria to preach about Jesus, and on a desert road he met an important official from Ethiopia reading the prophet Isaiah in his chariot. Philip explained the reading, and the man was baptised in water by the roadside. Lesson: a helper at the table can also be a teller of the Good News!
2027-04-01.special: First Thursday of Resurrection. Easter week, the week of the newly baptised.
term: Shamshana (deacon)

The Syriac word for a deacon, meaning ‘one who serves’; in Malayalam, Shemmashan. Deacons are ordained to serve at the altar, to proclaim the Gospel and to care for the poor, as the seven did in Acts 6.

family.explain: Jesus chose twelve friends and sent them out to tell people that God's kingdom was near. He gave them power to heal the sick. Then he told them: you got all this as a gift, so give it away as a gift! God has given us many gifts without asking anything back: our life, our family, his love, Baptism. We can give without asking anything back too: help at home without being asked, share a toy, be kind to someone who is lonely.
family.intention: We pray that our family may share freely the gifts God has given us.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing I can do for someone this week without wanting anything back?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Changanacherry the youth group ran the Easter food-kit distribution. Every family on the list received a kit. On the Thursday after Easter a girl in the group noticed an old woman sitting alone after the Holy Qurbana. She was a widow from a family that had moved from Tamil Nadu for work years ago; her name had never been put on the list, because no one in the parish committee knew her. Nobody had meant to forget her. The girl told the vicar, and he did not scold anyone. He called the youth together, read Acts 6 with them, and asked two of them to visit her every week. ‘The apostles had this problem in the first month of the Church,’ he said. ‘The answer was not a new rule. It was people full of the Spirit who would go and see.’ By Pentecost the widow was teaching the children a Tamil hymn to Our Lady.

pm.open: Risen Lord, you have given us everything without payment. Open our hands to give, and our hearts to welcome. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Enlarge the site of your tent (Isaiah 54:2). Whom is God asking me to make room for?
Their widows were being neglected (Acts 6:1). Who is being overlooked in my family or parish?
He set this aside, nailing it to the cross (Colossians 2:14). Do I still carry guilt that Christ has already erased?
You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8). What can I give freely this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us generous.
interc: For the deacons and seminarians of our eparchy, that they may be full of the Spirit and of wisdom.
For widows, widowers and the elderly who live alone, that the Church may never neglect them.
For the newly baptised, that they may live as people raised with Christ.
For migrants and those who worship far from their home, that they may find a welcome in our parishes.
For all who are sent to proclaim the Gospel, that they may bring peace into every house.
pm.close: Father, you made the barren one sing and widened the tent of your people. Keep us in your steadfast love, fill us with your Spirit, and send us to give freely what we have freely received. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Daniel: if God delivers us, good; but if not, we will not bow down. The young men walk singing in the fire.
Acts: Stephen, full of grace and power, faces false witnesses with the face of an angel.
Jesus: do not be afraid; everyone who acknowledges me before others, I will acknowledge before my Father.
2027-04-02.action: Make one small public act of acknowledgement of Christ today.
2027-04-02.question: Where am I tempted to keep quiet about Christ, and what would it cost me to speak?
kidsaint: Mar Shemun bar Sabbae

He was the chief bishop of the Christians in Persia about 1,700 years ago. The king ordered him to make the Christians pay a double tax and to worship the sun. Mar Shemun said he would not hurt his people and he would worship only God, the Maker of the sun. He was put to death together with many priests and believers, on Good Friday, the story says. Lesson: a good shepherd stays with his flock and stays with Jesus!
2027-04-02.special: First Friday of Resurrection: the Feast of Martyrs (All Saints in the East Syriac tradition). First Friday of the month. No abstinence today.
term: Sahda (martyr)

The Syriac word for a martyr, meaning ‘witness’, like the Greek martys. Kerala Christians know it from the name of Mar Geevarghese Sahada, St George the Martyr. Every Christian is called to be a witness; some are asked to give that witness with their blood.

family.explain: Jesus said that tiny sparrows are sold very cheaply, but God sees every one of them. And he even counts the hairs on your head! So we do not need to be afraid. Long ago some brave Christians, called martyrs, loved Jesus so much that they would not stop following him even when bad people hurt them. Today we remember them. We can be brave too: we can tell our friends that we love Jesus, and pray even when others are watching.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in places where it is dangerous to follow Jesus, that God may keep them brave and safe.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for me to say that I belong to Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A first-year engineering student from Kottayam shared a hostel room in Pune with three boys from other states. On his first Friday evening he went to a corner of the room, made the sign of the cross and began the night prayer his grandmother had taught him, almost in a whisper. One roommate laughed; another filmed it on his phone. For a week he prayed in the bathroom. Then he remembered the Gospel he had heard at the Feast of Martyrs: Do not be afraid. The next night he prayed in the room again, out loud. Nobody filmed it this time. Before the end of the term one of the roommates, who had not been inside a church since he was a child, asked if he could come along to the Holy Qurbana on Sunday. ‘You did not argue with us,’ he said. ‘You just kept praying.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, faithful witness, we gather with the great cloud of witnesses who surround us. Give us their courage and their joy. Amen. Alleluia!
share: But if not, we will not serve your gods (Daniel 3:18). Would my faith hold if God did not give me what I ask?
His face was like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). Does my face show that I have been with God?
He set out, not knowing where he was going (Hebrews 11:8). Where is God asking me to step out in faith?
Everyone who acknowledges me before others (Matthew 10:32). Where can I acknowledge Christ this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us your witnesses.
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith in every land, that the Lord may walk with them in the fire.
For the Church of the East and all the Churches of the Syriac tradition, heirs of the martyrs of Persia.
For those who are mocked or excluded at school or at work for their faith, that they may not be afraid.
For those who have hurt us, that we may forgive them as Stephen forgave.
For our dear departed, that they may join the saints in the city whose builder is God.
pm.close: Father, precious in your sight is the death of your faithful ones. Through the prayers of the martyrs and all the saints, keep us faithful, make us brave, and bring us to the city that has foundations. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: The women ask, “Who will roll away the stone?” and find it already rolled back.
The angel: he has been raised; he is not here; go, tell his disciples and Peter.
Paul: seek the things that are above; your life is hidden with Christ in God.
2027-04-03.action: Take one step today towards the ‘stone’ you have been dreading.
2027-04-03.question: What stone am I worrying about that God may already have moved?
catechism: The women and Peter, first witnesses.
Risen with Christ, hidden with him.
kidsaint: St Peter the Apostle

Peter loved Jesus, but on the night before Jesus died he was afraid and said three times, ‘I do not know him!’ Afterwards he cried bitterly. On Easter morning the angel said: go and tell the disciples and Peter. Jesus wanted Peter to know he was still his friend. Later Jesus made him the shepherd of the whole Church. Lesson: when you make a mistake, Jesus calls you back by name!
2027-04-03.special: First Saturday of Resurrection. The last day of Easter week, the week of the newly baptised.
term: Hadh b'Shabba (Sunday)

The Syriac name for Sunday, ‘the first day of the week’, the phrase the Gospels use for the morning of the Resurrection (Mark 16:2). For the East Syriac Church every Sunday is a little Easter, the day of the Risen Lord.

family.explain: Early on Sunday morning three women walked to Jesus' tomb. They were worried: “Who will roll away the big stone for us?” But when they got there, the stone was already rolled away! An angel in white said: “Jesus is not here. He is risen!” Sometimes we worry about things, but God is already there to help us. We can tell Jesus our worries, and trust him.
family.intention: We pray that our family may trust Jesus with all our worries, because he is risen and goes ahead of us.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one ‘big stone’ I am worried about? Let's give it to Jesus now.”

illus: An illustration

For three years a man in Thodupuzha had not spoken to his younger brother after a quarrel over a strip of rubber land. Every Easter his wife asked him to make peace, and every Easter he said, ‘He will throw me out.’ That year, on the Saturday after Easter, he finally walked the two kilometres to his brother's house, rehearsing what he would say. He stopped at the gate, almost turned back, and then saw that the gate was open and his brother was standing in the yard. ‘I was coming to you tomorrow, after the Qurbana,’ the brother said. ‘I have been wanting to for a year.’ They sat on the verandah until dark. On the way home the man laughed out loud. ‘The whole road I was asking who would roll away the stone,’ he told his wife, ‘and it was already open.’

pm.open: Risen Lord, you go ahead of us into every Galilee. Lift up our minds to you as we pray together. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Who will roll away the stone for us? (Mark 16:3). What am I afraid to face?
He has been raised; he is not here (Mark 16:6). How does the empty tomb change the way I look at death?
Go, tell his disciples and Peter (Mark 16:7). Do I believe that Christ calls me back after I have failed?
Your life is hidden with Christ in God (Colossians 3:3). Where do I see hidden holiness around me?
pm.resp: Lord, we seek you above all things.
interc: For those who are afraid of a stone in their lives, a confession, a reconciliation, an illness, that they may find it rolled away.
For all who have denied or abandoned the Lord, that they may hear him call them by name as he called Peter.
For the newly baptised, as Easter week ends, that their new life may continue hidden with Christ.
For mothers and grandmothers whose hidden prayers hold their families together.
For pilgrims going up to Malayattoor and to all the shrines of Mar Thoma this New Sunday.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son from the dead and seated him at your right hand. Keep our hearts fixed on him, forgive us when we fail, and on the last day reveal us with him in glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you?
The two disciples urge the stranger: Stay with us.
He took bread, blessed and broke it, and their eyes were opened.
2027-04-05.action: Tonight, pray: Lord, stay with us, because it is almost evening.
2027-04-05.question: Is there someone in my parish or family I have written off because they belong to ‘another side’?
catechism: The Emmaus pattern of the liturgy.
kidsaint: St Cleopas

Cleopas was one of the two disciples walking sadly to Emmaus. A stranger joined them, explained the Bible, and then broke bread at their table: it was Jesus! Cleopas ran all the way back to Jerusalem in the dark to tell the others. Lesson: when we meet Jesus, we can't keep the good news to ourselves!
2027-04-05.special: Second Monday of Resurrection. The Latin Church keeps the Annunciation today (transferred); Syro-Malabar faithful follow their eparchy.
term: Breaking of the Bread

One of the oldest names for the Holy Qurbana, used in Luke and Acts (Acts 2:42). It recalls how Jesus broke bread at the Last Supper and at Emmaus, and how the Church shares the one Bread that makes her one body.

family.explain: Two friends of Jesus were walking home, very sad. A man walked with them and explained the Bible. When they reached home they said, ‘Stay with us.’ At supper he broke the bread, and suddenly they saw: it was Jesus! He had risen! At Holy Qurbana Jesus breaks the bread for us too.
family.intention: We pray for families and parishes where people are quarrelling, that Jesus may make them one again.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we should make peace with this week? How can we do it?”

illus: An illustration

Two families in a parish near Changanassery had not spoken for six years after a quarrel over the parish feast committee. Each sat on a different side of the church. One Easter season the vicar asked both fathers to carry the canopy together in a small procession. They agreed only because the vicar asked. Walking side by side under the canopy, neither knew what to say. At the end one of them said quietly, ‘We were fighting about who should be in charge of a feast for the Lord, and we forgot the Lord.’ That evening the two families ate together for the first time in six years.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen and present among us, open the Scriptures to us and make our hearts burn within us. Stay with us. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Has Christ been divided? (1 Corinthians 1:13). Where do I take sides in a way that divides the Body of Christ?
Stay with us, because it is almost evening (Luke 24:29). Where do I need to invite the Lord into my evening?
He had been made known to them in the breaking of the bread (Luke 24:35). How do I meet the Risen Lord in the Holy Qurbana?
Were not our hearts burning within us? (Luke 24:32). When has the word of God set my heart on fire?
pm.resp: Lord, stay with us.
interc: For the unity of the Church, and especially for unity within our own Syro-Malabar Church.
For parishes and families divided by quarrels, that they may be reconciled at the one table of the Lord.
For all who walk away from the Church in sadness, that the Lord may walk with them and bring them home.
For priests, that they may open the Scriptures and break the bread with burning hearts.
For travellers and migrants on the road tonight.
pm.close: Father, your Son made himself known to his disciples in the breaking of the bread. Gather us into one around his table, heal our divisions, and send us out with burning hearts to tell what we have seen. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Saul, newly baptised, at once proclaims in the synagogues: Jesus is the Son of God.
His brothers lower him down the wall of Damascus in a basket.
Jesus: If you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me.
2027-04-06.action: Do one hidden act of kindness today and tell no one.
2027-04-06.question: Whose applause do I live for: God's, or other people's?
catechism: Jesus confessed as Son of God.
The Church and the Jewish people.
kidsaint: St Paul the Apostle

Before he met Jesus, Paul (called Saul) hurt Christians. After he met the Risen Jesus, he could not stop telling everyone, ‘Jesus is the Son of God!’ Some people wanted to hurt him, so his friends let him down over the city wall in a big basket at night. Lesson: Jesus can change anyone, and good friends help us when we are in danger!
term: Synagogue

From the Greek for ‘gathering’: the house where a Jewish community meets to pray and to hear the Law and the Prophets read and explained. Jesus taught in synagogues, and Paul preached first in them. The Church's own Liturgy of the Word grew from this practice of reading and explaining the Scriptures.

family.explain: Saul used to be against Jesus. But after Jesus met him, he became Jesus' friend and told everyone about him. Some people were angry and waited at the city gates to catch him. So his friends put him in a big basket and lowered him down the wall at night. He was safe! Jesus' family looks after each other.
family.intention: We pray for people who do not yet know Jesus, that they may meet him as Saul did.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is someone we could help this week, like Saul's friends helped him?”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolmaster in Pala spent the last years of his life reading the whole Bible from Genesis to Revelation, slowly, with a pencil. After his funeral his grandson opened that Bible and found, in the margins of the Old Testament, small crosses drawn beside hundreds of verses: the lamb of Abraham, the bronze serpent, the stone the builders rejected, the suffering Servant. On the first page he had written a single line in his careful hand: ‘Looking for him in every book. Found him.’ The grandson, who had not read the Bible since his First Holy Communion, began to read it again, following the crosses.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you opened the eyes of Saul and the Scriptures to your disciples. Open our hearts now to your word. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Immediately he began to proclaim Jesus (Acts 9:20). What holds me back from speaking of Jesus?
His disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall (Acts 9:25). Who has carried me in a time of danger, and whom can I carry?
How can you believe when you accept glory from one another? (John 5:44). Where am I living for the praise of others?
He wrote about me (John 5:46). Where have I found Christ in the Old Testament?
pm.resp: Lord, let us seek your glory alone.
interc: For all who persecute the Church, that they may meet the Risen Lord as Saul did.
For new Christians, that their first zeal may grow into lifelong faithfulness.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant, and for friendship between Christians and Jews.
For those in danger for their faith, that brothers and sisters may protect them.
For students of Scripture, catechists and Bible study groups in our parishes.
pm.close: Father, the Law and the Prophets speak of your Son, and in his Resurrection all your promises are fulfilled. Make us seek the glory that comes from you alone, and send us, like Paul, to proclaim that Jesus is your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: For freedom Christ has set us free; do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
What counts is faith working through love.
Jesus touches a deaf man's ears and tongue and says: Ephphatha, Be opened.
2027-04-07.action: Before the Gospel at your next Holy Qurbana, pray: Lord, open my ears and my lips.
2027-04-07.question: Is my faith only something I hold, or something that works through love?
kidsaint: St Francis de Sales

St Francis de Sales was a kind bishop who met a deaf man named Martin. Nobody had taught Martin about God, so Francis learned to talk with him using signs, taught him about Jesus, and prepared him for Holy Communion. Lesson: Jesus wants everyone to hear about him, and we can find new ways to share his love!
term: Ephphatha

An Aramaic word, the language Jesus spoke, meaning ‘Be opened’. Mark keeps the very word Jesus said to the deaf man. In the ancient baptismal rites, and still in the Latin rite of Baptism, the minister touches the ears and mouth of the one being baptised and says Ephphatha, praying that he may soon hear God's word and profess the faith.

family.explain: Some people brought a man who could not hear or speak well to Jesus. Jesus took him away from the crowd, touched his ears and his tongue, looked up to heaven and said, ‘Ephphatha!’ That means ‘Be opened!’ At once the man could hear and speak. Jesus wants to open our ears to hear God and our mouths to say kind words and to praise him.
family.intention: We pray for people who cannot hear or speak, and for those who help them.
family.ask: Ask: “What kind words can we say to each other today with the mouths Jesus gave us?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Thrissur a catechist noticed that a ten-year-old boy in her class never answered and seemed to understand nothing. The other children laughed at him. She learned that he had been born deaf, and that no one had ever explained the faith to him in a way he could follow. That year she went for evening classes in sign language. Months later, at his First Holy Communion, the boy stood at the front and signed the Our Father while the whole congregation prayed it aloud. Many in the church were weeping. Afterwards his grandmother said to the catechist, ‘For ten years we thought God could not reach him. You opened the door.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, say over us your word Ephphatha: open our ears to your word and our lips to your praise. Amen. Alleluia!
share: For freedom Christ has set us free (Galatians 5:1). What still holds me in slavery?
The only thing that counts is faith working through love (Galatians 5:6). Where does my faith need to become love?
He took him aside in private, away from the crowd (Mark 7:33). Do I let Jesus take me aside to heal me?
He has done everything well (Mark 7:37). What has the Lord done well in my life this Easter?
pm.resp: Lord, open our ears and our lips.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the freedom of the Gospel to all peoples.
For those who are enslaved by addiction, debt or fear, that the Risen Lord may release them.
For deaf people and those with speech difficulties, and for all who teach and serve them.
For catechists, that they may find ways to open the faith to every child.
For ourselves, that our faith may work through love.
pm.close: Father, through your Son you broke our chains and opened our ears to your word. Keep us standing firm in the freedom of your children, and let our faith bear fruit in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: Live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ.
Suffering for Christ is a privilege granted like faith itself.
The Canaanite mother: Lord, help me. Jesus: Woman, great is your faith!
2027-04-08.action: Every time you feel anxious today, pray: Lord, help me.
2027-04-08.question: Do I give up praying when God seems silent?
catechism: Jesus hears the prayer of faith.
kidsaint: St Monica

St Monica's son Augustine did not believe in Jesus and lived a wrong life. For many years Monica prayed and cried for him every day. She never gave up. At last Augustine became a Christian, a bishop and a great saint! Lesson: like the mother in today's Gospel, never stop praying for the people you love.
term: Canaanite

The old name for the peoples who lived in the land before Israel. Mark calls this woman a Syrophoenician; Matthew calls her a Canaanite to show that she is a complete outsider to Israel. Her great faith shows that the Gospel is for every nation.

family.explain: A mother came to Jesus because her daughter was very sick. At first Jesus did not answer. But she did not give up. She knelt down and said, ‘Lord, help me!’ Jesus was so happy with her faith that he healed her daughter. When we pray, we should keep trusting Jesus, even when we have to wait.
family.intention: We pray for children who are sick, and for their mothers and fathers.
family.ask: Ask: “What is something we have been praying for? Let us not give up!”

illus: An illustration

For three years a Hindu mother from a village near Kottayam came every Tuesday evening to a small church and sat quietly at the back. Her daughter had a serious illness, and the doctors had little hope. She did not know the prayers, but she would fold her hands and say in Malayalam, ‘Help me.’ The sacristan, who had been asked many times by others why she was allowed to stay, always answered, ‘Jesus never sent a mother away.’ When her daughter recovered enough to go back to college, the mother brought a garland of jasmine and laid it before the crucifix, wept, and went home. She still comes on Tuesdays, she says, to say thank you.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. We come to you as the Canaanite mother came, kneeling and trusting. Help us. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ (Philippians 1:27). Where does my conduct not yet match the Gospel?
He has graciously granted you the privilege… of suffering for him (Philippians 1:29). How can I offer a present suffering to Christ?
But he did not answer her at all (Matthew 15:23). How do I respond when God seems silent?
Woman, great is your faith! (Matthew 15:28). Whom do I need to keep praying for?
pm.resp: Lord, help us.
interc: For Christians who suffer for their faith, that they may stand firm and be unafraid.
For mothers and fathers who pray for sick or wandering children, that they may not lose heart.
For people of other religions who seek God with a sincere heart.
For the mission of the Church to all nations, in the footsteps of Saint Thomas.
For ourselves, that we may live in a manner worthy of the Gospel.
pm.close: Father, your Son heard the cry of a mother from a foreign land and praised her faith. Give us that faith which does not give up, and feed us at the table of your children. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: The message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us it is the power of God.
We proclaim Christ crucified, the power of God and the wisdom of God.
A sower went out to sow; the seed in good soil yields a hundredfold.
2027-04-09.action: Spend five minutes today before a crucifix and thank the Lord.
2027-04-09.question: What kind of ground does God's word find in me today?
catechism: The power of God in the Cross.
kidsaint: St Alphonsa

St Alphonsa of Bharananganam was often sick and in pain. Instead of complaining, she offered her sufferings to Jesus with love, like a seed planted in the ground. Today she is the first woman saint of India, and many people pray at her tomb. Lesson: when we offer even our hurts to Jesus, he can make them grow into something beautiful!
term: Parable

From the Greek parabolē, ‘something placed beside’: a short story from ordinary life placed beside the mystery of God's Kingdom to help us understand it. Jesus' parables invite the listener to decide; that is why he ends, “Let anyone with ears to hear listen!”

family.explain: A farmer threw seeds everywhere. Some fell on the path and birds ate them. Some fell on rocks and dried up. Some fell among thorns and got choked. But some fell on good soil and grew into a big harvest! Jesus says God's word is like seed. When we listen and keep it in our hearts, it grows.
family.intention: We pray for farmers, and for all who teach God's word to children.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make our hearts good soil for Jesus' word this week?”

illus: An illustration

A Sunday school teacher in a hill parish in Idukki taught catechism for over forty years. She sometimes said that most of her pupils forgot everything the week after their Confirmation, and she wondered if her work was worth it. In her eightieth year a letter came from a priest working among tribal villages in Madhya Pradesh. He had been the noisiest boy in her class, the one she had once sent out of the room. ‘You told us that the seed is never wasted,’ he wrote. ‘I did not listen then. But it stayed in me. Today I baptised thirty-two people. This harvest is yours too.’ She kept the letter in her Bible until she died.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, crucified and risen, sow your word in our hearts now, and make them good soil. Amen. Alleluia!
share: For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing (1 Corinthians 1:18). Do I ever feel embarrassed by the Cross?
Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:24). Where do I look for power and wisdom apart from Christ?
Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it (Mark 4:7). What thorns choke God's word in me?
Thirty and sixty and a hundredfold (Mark 4:8). What fruit is the Lord asking of me this Easter?
pm.resp: Lord, make us good soil for your word.
interc: For preachers and catechists, that they may sow the word generously without losing heart.
For those who find the Cross foolish, that they may discover in it the power and love of God.
For farmers in Kerala and throughout India, for good rains and a just reward for their labour.
For those whose faith is choked by worry or wealth, that they may make room for God again.
For the Church in North India and all mission lands, that the seed of the Gospel may bear a hundredfold.
pm.close: Father, in the foolishness of the Cross you revealed your power and wisdom, and in the Resurrection you brought forth the harvest. Make our hearts good soil, and let your word bear fruit in us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: Above all, clothe yourselves with love; let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; sing to God with gratitude.
The Risen Lord: Touch me and see; and he ate a piece of broiled fish before them.
2027-04-10.action: Gather your family for evening prayer tonight, light the lamp, and sing one hymn together.
2027-04-10.question: Does the word of Christ live in my home, or only visit on Sundays?
catechism: The real body of the Risen Lord.
kidsaint: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara

St Chavara Achan was a priest in Kerala who loved families. He told parents to pray together every day with their children, and he wrote a letter of advice for families that is still read today. He also started schools so that every child could learn. Lesson: a family that prays together is a little church where Jesus lives!
2027-04-10.special: Second Saturday of Resurrection. Saturday is dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary.
term: Qurbana

A Syriac word meaning ‘offering’: the name the Syro-Malabar Church gives to the Holy Eucharist, the offering of Christ to the Father, made present on the altar, in which the faithful offer themselves with him. The Greek name Eucharist means ‘thanksgiving’. Both names together describe a Christian life: an offering made with thanks.

family.explain: On Easter evening Jesus came to his friends and said, ‘Peace be with you.’ They were scared and thought he was a ghost! Jesus said, ‘Look at my hands and feet. Touch me! A ghost doesn't have a body like me.’ Then he ate some fish in front of them. Jesus really rose from the dead, with his real body!
family.intention: We pray for families, that they may pray and sing together every day.
family.ask: Ask: “What hymn shall we sing together at our prayer tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A Malayali family working in Kuwait found that their children were losing the habit of prayer: school, homework and screens filled every evening. The father decided to keep one rule. At half past seven the lamp was lit, the television switched off, and the family sat down for evening prayer, with the grandparents in Kerala joining by video call. Some evenings it was only ten minutes: a decade of the rosary, a short Gospel reading and one hymn the grandmother loved. Years later the eldest daughter, at university in Canada, wrote home: ‘At half past seven I still light a candle. When I sing that hymn I can hear Ammachi's voice, and I know I am not alone.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen in your true body, stand among us now and say to us: Peace be with you. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Above all, clothe yourselves with love (Colossians 3:14). Which virtue is falling off me for lack of love?
Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts (Colossians 3:15). Where do I need to let his peace make the call?
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly (Colossians 3:16). Does God's word have a room in my house?
Touch me and see (Luke 24:39). How does my faith in the bodily Resurrection change how I treat my body and others?
pm.resp: Lord, let your peace rule in our hearts.
interc: For Christian families, that they may be little churches of prayer, Scripture and song.
For families scattered by migration, that faith may keep them united.
For those who doubt the Resurrection, that the Risen Lord may stand among them.
For our beloved dead, that they may rise in glory on the last day.
For choirs and all who lead the singing in our parishes.
pm.close: Father, your Son rose in his true body and showed his wounds to his disciples. Make us thankful in all things, let the word of Christ dwell in our homes, and bring us with all your saints to the resurrection of the body. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: James: be patient like the farmer who waits for the rains, and do not grumble against one another.
Ten bridesmaids waited for the bridegroom; all slept, but only five had oil.
The Risen Lord is the Bridegroom; keep the lamp of Baptism burning.
2027-04-12.action: Light a lamp or candle at the family prayer this evening and pray for one person you are tempted to grumble against.
2027-04-12.question: What keeps the oil in my lamp, and what is letting it run dry?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about ten girls waiting for a bridegroom at night. They all had lamps. Five took extra oil, and five did not. When the bridegroom came at midnight, the lamps of five girls were going out! Jesus wants our hearts to be like lamps full of oil: full of prayer and kindness, so that we are always ready to meet him.
family.intention: We pray that every member of our family may keep the light of Jesus burning in the heart.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing that puts oil in the lamp of our hearts?”

illus: An illustration

An old woman in a village near Pala kept a small brass lamp in the corner of her room for more than sixty years. Every evening she filled it, trimmed the wick and lit it before the evening prayer, even in the years when she prayed alone. When her grandson, an engineer in Bengaluru, asked why she still did it when there was electric light, she said: “The lamp is not for the room. It is to remind me that he can come tonight, and I want him to find the house awake.” She died on an Easter Monday, and the lamp was still burning beside her bed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Bridegroom of our souls, we gather with our lamps. Fill them with the oil of your Spirit. Amen. Alleluia!
share: The farmer waits for the precious crop from the earth (James 5:7). Where is God asking me to be patient?
Beloved, do not grumble against one another (James 5:9). Against whom do I grumble most often?
When the foolish took their lamps, they took no oil with them (Matthew 25:3). Is there oil in my lamp?
Keep awake therefore (Matthew 25:13). How can I live today as a day on which the Lord might come?
pm.resp: Lord, keep our lamps burning.
interc: For the Church, the bride of Christ, that she may wait for her Lord with joy and readiness.
For farmers and labourers who wait for rain and wages, that they may find patience and justice.
For families divided by grumbling and quarrels, that they may find peace.
For those who have let the lamp of faith grow dim, that the Risen Lord may light it again.
For our group, that we may be found awake when the Bridegroom comes.
pm.close: Father, your Son rose from the dead and will come again as the Bridegroom of his Church. Give us patient hearts and burning lamps, so that we may go in with him to the wedding feast. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Respect those who labour among you; encourage the fainthearted and help the weak.
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; do not quench the Spirit.
The seed of the word is good; the soil of our hearts decides the harvest.
2027-04-13.action: Thank one person who serves your parish, by name, this week.
2027-04-13.question: Which part of my heart is path, rock or thorns, and what will I do about it?

family.explain: Jesus said that God's word is like seed. Some seed falls on a hard path and birds take it. Some falls on rocks and dries up. Some falls among thorns and is choked. But some falls on good soil and grows into a big harvest! When we listen to Jesus and do what he says, our hearts become good soil.
family.intention: We pray for our catechism teachers and all who teach us God's word.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week so that Jesus' words grow in our family?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in a parish near Thrissur taught the same class of ten-year-olds for twenty-six years. Most of her pupils forgot her name. One Easter a young priest, newly ordained, came to say his first Qurbana in the parish. After the Qurbana he went straight to the back of the church, found the old teacher, and knelt for her blessing. In front of everyone he said that the first time he had ever wanted to be a priest was in her class, when she told them that God's word is a seed that grows even when no one is watching.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen Sower, scatter your word in our hearts as we gather, and make us good soil. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Esteem them very highly in love because of their work (1 Thessalonians 5:13). Whom do I need to thank in my parish?
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing (1 Thessalonians 5:16–17). What steals my joy and my prayer?
Do not quench the Spirit (1 Thessalonians 5:19). Where am I resisting the Holy Spirit?
The cares of the world, and the lure of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word (Mark 4:19). What is choking the word in me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us good soil.
interc: For our bishops, priests, religious and catechism teachers, that they may be held in love because of their work.
For the fainthearted and the weak in our parish, that they may find encouragement and help.
For those whose Easter joy has met trouble, that it may put down deep roots.
For those choked by worries about money, exams, debts and prices, that they may find peace.
For our group, that the word may bear fruit in us a hundredfold.
pm.close: Father, your Son sows his word in every heart. Make our hearts good soil, keep us joyful, prayerful and thankful, and do not let us quench your Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul in prison: for me, living is Christ and dying is gain.
He longs to be with Christ, yet stays for the progress and joy of his people.
Jesus touches a leper and says: I do choose; be made clean.
2027-04-14.action: Visit or call one person who is lonely because of illness, age or shame.
2027-04-14.question: What is my life really built on, and whom do I keep at a distance?

family.explain: Long ago, people with a skin disease called leprosy had to live far away from everyone. No one would touch them. One day a man with leprosy knelt before Jesus and said: if you want, you can make me clean. Jesus did not run away. He reached out and touched him, and said: I want to; be clean! And the man was healed. Jesus loves to reach out to people whom others leave alone.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick and lonely, and for those who care for them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our school, church or neighbourhood is often left alone? How can we reach out to them?”

illus: An illustration

A Syro-Malabar sister from Kottayam worked for nineteen years in a leprosy home in a village of Bihar. In her first week an old man with no fingers held out his hand to her, and she hesitated. He pulled it back and laughed, without bitterness: “Everyone does that, Sister.” That night she could not sleep. The next morning she went straight to him, took both his hands in hers and held them while she said good morning. When she was transferred years later, the residents came to the gate to send her off. The old man was no longer alive, but his son, who had no leprosy, was there. He told her: “My father said you were the first person in thirty years who touched him first.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen and living, you are our life. Stretch out your hand over us as we gather. Amen. Alleluia!
share: For to me, living is Christ (Philippians 1:21). What would I honestly put in place of Christ in that sentence?
My desire is to depart and be with Christ (Philippians 1:23). How do I think and feel about my own death?
Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean (Matthew 8:2). What do I need to bring to Jesus to be made clean?
He stretched out his hand and touched him (Matthew 8:3). Whom am I keeping at a distance?
pm.resp: Lord, stretch out your hand.
interc: For Christians in prison and in danger for their faith, that they may share Paul's peace.
For the dying, that they may go to Christ with trust and be surrounded by love.
For people with leprosy and other illnesses that bring isolation, and for all who care for them.
For those ashamed of their sins, that they may come to the sacrament of Reconciliation and hear the Lord say, I do choose.
For our group, that Christ may be our life.
pm.close: Father, your Son is our life and our resurrection. Deliver us from the fear of death, and make us his hands reaching out to all who are shut out. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: The poor Macedonians gave with joy beyond their means, because they first gave themselves to the Lord.
Christ was rich, yet for our sake became poor, so that we might become rich.
Jesus, asleep in the boat, rises and calms the storm: Why are you afraid?
2027-04-15.action: Set aside a small daily gift for the poor this week, like the old custom of the handful of rice.
2027-04-15.question: What storm is frightening me, and is fear keeping my hands closed?

family.explain: One night Jesus and his friends were in a boat. A big storm came, and the waves splashed into the boat. Jesus was sleeping! The disciples woke him and cried: don't you care? Jesus stood up and said to the wind and the sea: Peace! Be still! And everything became calm. When we are afraid, we can call Jesus. He is always with us.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and all who work at sea, and for people facing storms in their lives.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes us afraid? Let us tell Jesus about it together now.”

illus: An illustration

In August 2018, when the rivers of central Kerala overflowed, a fisherman from the coast near Thiruvananthapuram loaded his boat on a lorry and drove inland with his son and two neighbours. For four days they rowed through flooded streets, lifting the old and the sick out of upstairs windows. On the third night, in rain and darkness, the boat was caught by a strong current and nearly overturned. His son was terrified.
