The fisherman held the gunwale with one hand, made the sign of the cross with the other, and said only: “He is in the boat. Row.” They reached the roof where a family of seven was waiting. Afterwards, when people offered to pay him, he refused. “The sea gives us our living,” he said. “This time we gave something back.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, master of wind and sea, you are in our boat. Speak your peace over us as we gather. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Their abundant joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in a wealth of generosity (2 Corinthians 8:2). Is my giving generous or grudging?
They gave themselves first to the Lord (2 Corinthians 8:5). Have I given myself to him before I give my money?
Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? (Mark 4:38). What storm am I in now?
Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith? (Mark 4:40). What would trust look like in my situation?
pm.resp: Lord, speak your peace.
interc: For the Church, the boat of Christ, that she may cross every storm with him on board.
For the poor and for all who give generously from their poverty.
For fishermen and seafarers, and for families waiting for them on the shore.
For people overwhelmed by illness, debt, grief or persecution, that they may hear the Lord say, Peace! Be still!
For our group, that we may give ourselves first to the Lord.
pm.close: Father, your Son became poor for our sake and rules the wind and the sea. Make us generous in want and calm in danger, because he is with us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: The strong must bear with the weak and please their neighbour, because Christ did not please himself.
Paul prays that we may live in harmony and glorify God with one voice.
Jesus heals a withered hand on the sabbath: it is lawful to do good.
2027-04-16.action: Be patient this week with one person whose weakness irritates you.
2027-04-16.question: Do I use my freedom to build others up, and do I let rules or pride keep me from doing good?

family.explain: A man had a hand that could not move. Jesus saw him in the synagogue and said: come and stand here. Then he said: stretch out your hand! The man tried, and his hand was healed. Some people were angry because it was the day of rest. But Jesus showed that God's holy day is the best day to do good.
family.intention: We pray for people who cannot work because of illness or injury.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing can our family do together next Sunday after Holy Qurbana?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Changanacherry two neighbouring families had not spoken for eleven years after a quarrel over a boundary wall. Both sat in the same church every Sunday, on opposite sides. One Sunday the Epistle was Paul's prayer that the community might glorify God with one voice. After the Qurbana the older of the two men, who had been the stronger in the quarrel and had won the case, crossed the churchyard to the other man, who was now partly paralysed after a stroke. He did not mention the wall. He said: “Your hand is weak now. Let me help you to the car.” The next week the two families sat together for the first time.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you did not please yourself. Gather us in harmony now, so that we may praise the Father with one voice. Amen. Alleluia!
share: We who are strong ought to put up with the failings of the weak (Romans 15:1). Whose weakness do I find hard to bear?
Whatever was written in former days was written for our instruction (Romans 15:4). How do the Scriptures give me hope?
Come and stand here (Luke 6:8). What part of my life is withered and needs to be brought to Jesus?
Is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath? (Luke 6:9). How do I keep the Lord's Day?
pm.resp: Lord, make us one in you.
interc: For the Church, that she may live in harmony and glorify God with one voice.
For our Syro-Malabar Church and all Churches, that disagreements may be healed in patience and love.
For people disabled by illness or injury, and for those who cannot earn their bread.
For families and neighbours divided by quarrels, that the strong may take the first step.
For our group, that we may keep the Lord's Day holy with works of mercy.
pm.close: Father, your Son bore our insults and healed the withered hand. Make us patient with the weak, united in praise, and quick to do good on your holy day. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: James: kind words without help are useless; faith without works is dead.
Jesus: why call me Lord, Lord, and not do what I say?
The one who hears and acts builds on rock; the flood cannot shake that house.
2027-04-17.action: Do one concrete act of help for a person in need this week, not only a promise to pray.
2027-04-17.question: Where do I call Jesus Lord without doing what he tells me?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about two men who built houses. One dug deep and built on strong rock. The other built on soft ground. When a big flood came, the house on soft ground fell down, but the house on the rock stood strong! Jesus says that when we listen to him and do what he says, we are building our life on rock.
family.intention: We pray for families whose homes were damaged by floods or landslides, and for all who have no home.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus asks us to do that we can do together this week?”

illus: An illustration

After the landslides in Idukki, a team visited the hillsides to see which houses had survived. On one slope every house had slipped or cracked except one, a plain old house built by a farmer in the 1970s. His son explained that his father had refused to build until he reached solid rock, though it took two extra months of digging and the neighbours laughed at him. “He used to say the same thing about faith,” the son added. “Anyone can build a church on Sunday. The digging is Monday to Saturday.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen rock and cornerstone, we come to hear your words. Give us grace to act on them. Amen. Alleluia!
share: What good is it if you say you have faith but do not have works? (James 2:14). Where is my faith only words?
Go in peace; keep warm and eat your fill (James 2:16). Whom am I sending away with words alone?
Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell you? (Luke 6:46). What has Jesus told me to do that I have not done?
He dug deeply and laid the foundation on rock (Luke 6:48). What is my life built on?
pm.resp: Lord, make us doers of your word.
interc: For the Church, that her faith may be alive in works of love.
For the hungry, the homeless and those without clothing, and for those who serve them.
For families who have lost their homes in floods and landslides.
For those whose lives are shaken by sickness, failure or grief, that they may stand firm on Christ.
For our group, that like the Blessed Virgin Mary we may hear the word of God and do it.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the rock on which we build. Make us hear his words and act on them, and let our faith be alive in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: keep the commandment without spot until the appearing of Christ, who made the good confession before Pilate.
Paul: God alone has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light.
Jesus: the owner sent his beloved son; the tenants killed him; God makes the rejected stone the cornerstone.
2027-04-19.action: Say the Creed slowly once today, as your own good confession.
2027-04-19.question: When the Owner of the vineyard sends for the fruit, what will he find in my life?
catechism: No collective blame for the Passion.
kidsaint: St Timothy

Timothy was a young man when Paul chose him as a helper. His grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice taught him the Scriptures when he was a child. Paul made him the leader of the Church in Ephesus and wrote him letters full of advice. Lesson: what you learn about Jesus at home can make you a helper of the whole Church!
2027-04-19.special: Fourth Monday of Resurrection. The day after the Sunday of prayer for vocations.
term: Good confession

Paul's name for a public statement of faith made before witnesses. Jesus made it before Pilate; Timothy made it, probably at his Baptism; every Christian makes it at Baptism and renews it in the Creed. In Greek the word is homologia, ‘saying the same thing’: saying with our lips what God has said to us.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a man who planted a lovely vineyard and let some farmers look after it. When it was time for the grapes, he sent helpers to collect his share, but the farmers were rude and sent them away. At last he sent his own dear son. The farmers did a very bad thing to him. Jesus was telling us about himself: God sent his Son, and people did not welcome him. But God raised Jesus from the dead! Now God has given us his vineyard, the Church, to look after.
family.intention: We pray for all the people who look after God's Church: our bishop, our priests, our parents and our teachers.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit can we give God this week? Let us choose one kind thing to do together.”

illus: An illustration

A farmer near Thodupuzha inherited a small rubber and pepper garden from his father. For years he left it to a caretaker and visited only to collect the money. When the caretaker grew careless, the vines withered and the trees were tapped badly. The farmer's son, home from the Gulf, began to walk through the garden every morning before work, clearing weeds and tying up the pepper vines. Within two seasons the garden was giving fruit again. The father said, “It was always the same land. What changed was that someone loved it enough to tend it.” The vineyard of the Church is like that: it gives fruit where someone tends it each day with love.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, beloved Son of the Father, rejected by the builders and raised as the cornerstone, gather us now in your vineyard and teach us to bear fruit. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Christ Jesus, who in his testimony before Pontius Pilate made the good confession (1 Timothy 6:13). When have I found it hard to speak the truth about my faith?
He dwells in unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16). How do I show reverence for God in prayer and in church?
I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him (Luke 20:13). Where has God sent messengers into my life, and how have I received them?
The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone (Psalm 118:22). Where have I seen God bring good out of rejection?
pm.resp: Lord, make us fruitful in your vineyard.
interc: For our bishops and priests, the tenants God has placed over his vineyard, that they may be faithful and generous.
For all who are called to the priesthood and religious life, that they may answer with courage.
For Christians who suffer for the faith, that they may make the good confession with the peace of Christ.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that he may bless them in his faithfulness.
For our families and parishes, that they may bear the fruit of faith, mercy and justice.
pm.close: Father, you sent your beloved Son into the vineyard, and when he was rejected you raised him to be the cornerstone. Make us faithful in our confession and fruitful in our works, until he comes again in glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: the rich must not hope in uncertain riches, but in God who richly provides; they must be rich in good works.
Paul: Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you.
Jesus: it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle; but for God all things are possible.
2027-04-20.action: Give something away today before you buy anything for yourself.
2027-04-20.question: Where is my hope really placed: in what I own, or in God?
kidsaint: St Antony of Egypt

Antony was a young man with rich fields in Egypt. One day in church he heard the words of Jesus: “go, sell your possessions, and give the money to the poor”. He did exactly that, cared for his younger sister, and went to pray in the desert. Many people came to him for advice, and he lived to be very old, full of joy. Lesson: when you give things away for Jesus, your heart becomes rich!
term: Deposit of faith

From Paul's word to Timothy, ‘guard what has been entrusted to you’ (the deposit). It means the whole of the faith handed down by the apostles in Scripture and Tradition, which the Church does not invent or change but guards, explains and hands on.

family.explain: Jesus said something very surprising: it is easier for a big camel to go through the tiny hole of a sewing needle than for a rich person to get into heaven. Can a camel do that? No! The disciples were shocked and asked, “Then who can be saved?” Jesus said, “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.” Only God can make our hearts open and good, and he wants to!
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough food or money, and for all of us, that we may learn to share.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one toy or thing we could give away to someone who needs it?”

illus: An illustration

An elderly widow in Kuttanad had a small paddy field and a few coconut trees. When she died, her grandchildren expected to find savings hidden in the house, as people said she had never spent much on herself. They found almost nothing: a rosary, her prayer book, and a notebook. In it, year after year, she had written the names of children whose school fees she had paid, families she had helped after the floods, and a seminarian whose cassock she had bought. At her funeral, people they had never seen came from three villages. One of the grandsons said, “We were looking for her treasure in a tin box. She had stored it somewhere else.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, for you all things are possible. Open our hearts, make us generous, and fill us with the life that really is life. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Not to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but rather on God (1 Timothy 6:17). What do I worry about losing most?
So that they may take hold of the life that really is life (1 Timothy 6:19). What in my life only looks like life?
Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you (1 Timothy 6:20). How am I handing on the faith to the next generation?
For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible (Matthew 19:26). What have I stopped asking God for?
pm.resp: Lord, for you all things are possible.
interc: For those who are rich, that they may be rich in good works, generous and ready to share.
For the poor and the unemployed, that they may find work, help and dignity.
For our bishops, priests and catechists, that they may guard and hand on the faith with fidelity and joy.
For those who have left home and family to follow Christ, that they may receive the hundredfold he promised.
For ourselves, that we may hope in God and not in what passes.
pm.close: Father, you richly provide us with everything, and in your Son's Resurrection you have begun the renewal of all things. Deliver us from the love of money, make us generous, and keep us faithful to the faith entrusted to us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Hebrews: Melchizedek, king of righteousness and peace, with no beginning or end recorded, resembles the Son of God and remains a priest forever.
Hebrews: the Levitical priests died; Christ is the one of whom it is testified that he lives.
Jesus: John, my works and the Father himself testify that the Father has sent me.
2027-04-21.action: Pray today for the priest who baptised you and for your parish priest.
2027-04-21.question: Do my works bear witness that the Father has sent his Son?
kidsaint: St Anselm

Anselm grew up in the mountains of northern Italy. As a child he dreamed of climbing up to God's palace on the mountain top. He became a monk, a great teacher and finally Archbishop of Canterbury in England. He loved to think about God, and said that we believe so that we may understand. Lesson: you can use your mind to love God more!
2027-04-21.special: Fourth Wednesday of Resurrection. Latin calendar: St Anselm.
term: Order of Melchizedek

A phrase from Psalm 110:4, used by the Letter to the Hebrews for the priesthood of Christ. It is not a priesthood inherited by birth, as in the tribe of Levi, but an eternal priesthood given by God's oath. Christ is priest by who he is, the eternal Son, and he exercises it for ever as the Risen One.

family.explain: Long ago, when Abraham was coming home from a battle, a king called Melchizedek came to meet him. He brought bread and wine and blessed Abraham. He was a priest of God. The Bible says he was like a picture of Jesus. Jesus is our priest for ever. At the Holy Qurbana, bread and wine are brought to the altar, and Jesus makes them his own Body and Blood.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, and for boys whom God is calling to be priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What does our priest do for us at the Holy Qurbana? Let us thank God for him tonight.”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Kochi, working abroad, rarely went to church. One night his father phoned from the hospital: his mother had had a stroke. He could not get a flight for two days. Unable to sleep, he found a small chapel near his apartment and sat in the back. He did not know what to pray. On the wall was a line from Hebrews: ‘He always lives to make intercession for them.’ He said later, “For the first time I understood that I did not have to find the words. Someone was already praying for my mother, and for me.” His mother recovered slowly. He still keeps a card with that verse in his wallet.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, our eternal Priest, you live for ever to intercede for us. Pray with us now, and make our prayer one with yours before the Father. Amen. Alleluia!
share: King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine (Genesis 14:18). What does the Holy Qurbana mean to me this week?
Resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever (Hebrews 7:3). How do I thank God for the priests in my life?
One of whom it is testified that he lives (Hebrews 7:8). Do I pray as one who believes Jesus is alive and listening?
The very works that I am doing, testify on my behalf (John 5:36). What works in my life bear witness to Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, eternal Priest, intercede for us.
interc: For our Holy Father the Pope, our Major Archbishop, our bishops and all priests, that they may serve faithfully at the altar.
For young men discerning a call to the priesthood, that they may hear and answer generously.
For those who cannot pray because of pain or despair, that Christ's intercession may carry them.
For those who seek the truth, that they may see the works of Christ in his Church and believe.
For ourselves, that we may be burning and shining lamps for Christ.
pm.close: Father, you made your Son a priest for ever according to the order of Melchizedek, and you raised him to live for ever interceding for us. Hear the prayer he makes for us, and make us faithful witnesses to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Peter: false teachers will come secretly and deny the Master who bought them.
Peter: because of them the way of truth will be maligned; in greed they will exploit with deceptive words.
Jesus: you make void the word of God for your tradition; this people honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
2027-04-22.action: Do one concrete act of care for your parents or an elderly relative today.
2027-04-22.question: Is there a custom in my life that has become a way to avoid love?
kidsaint: St Thomas the Apostle

Thomas was one of the twelve apostles. When he saw the Risen Jesus he said, “My Lord and my God!” The Christians of Kerala believe he came to India and taught our ancestors about Jesus. For hundreds of years they kept his faith carefully and handed it to their children. Lesson: the faith you learn at home is a treasure passed down from the apostles!
term: Korban

A Hebrew word meaning ‘offering’ or ‘gift dedicated to God’. Mark's Gospel uses it in the parallel passage (Mark 7:11). Jesus criticises the misuse of such a vow to avoid supporting one's parents: no religious practice can cancel the commandment of love.

family.explain: Some people asked Jesus why his friends did not wash their hands in a special religious way before eating. Jesus said that some people used religious rules to avoid looking after their own mother and father! He said: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” That means saying nice prayers is good, but God also wants us to really love, especially at home.
family.intention: We pray for grandparents and all old people, especially those who are lonely.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week to make Ammachi and Appachan, or an old neighbour, happy?”

illus: An illustration

A man in Changanassery was known in his parish as a pillar of the church: he never missed the Sunday Qurbana, led the prayer group and organised the feast. His old father lived alone in the ancestral house a few kilometres away, and the son visited him only at Christmas and Easter. One Lent the vicar spoke about the Gospel of today, and the man went home uneasy. The next evening he drove to his father's house and found him sitting alone on the veranda in the dark. He sat beside him and they said the rosary together. After that he went every Thursday. He said later, “I had been honouring God with my lips. My father taught me where my heart had been missing.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you bought us with your Blood. Draw our hearts near to you now, so that our prayer may be more than words. Amen. Alleluia!
share: They will even deny the Master who bought them (2 Peter 2:1). What voices in my life lead me away from Christ?
Because of these teachers the way of truth will be maligned (2 Peter 2:2). Does my way of life make the faith attractive or not?
For the sake of your tradition, you make void the word of God (Matthew 15:6). Have I used any custom to avoid a duty of love?
This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Matthew 15:8). How can my heart be nearer to God in prayer?
pm.resp: Lord, draw our hearts near to you.
interc: For the Church, that she may remain faithful to the faith of the apostles and teach it with love.
For those who have been led astray by false teachings, that they may find their way back to Christ.
For elderly parents who are neglected or lonely, that their children may honour and care for them.
For all who use religion for gain, that they may repent.
For ourselves, that our worship may come from the heart.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to buy us back with his Blood, and you call us to worship you in spirit and truth. Keep us in the faith of the apostles, and give us hearts that love you and honour those you have given us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.
Paul: be filled with the Spirit, singing and giving thanks at all times and for everything.
Jesus: You give them something to eat; he took, blessed, broke and gave the loaves, and all were filled.
2027-04-23.action: Give thanks before every meal today, slowly, as Jesus did.
2027-04-23.question: What small loaves do I have that Jesus could use to feed someone?
kidsaint: St Teresa of Kolkata

Mother Teresa saw poor people dying alone on the streets of Kolkata. She began with almost nothing: a few rupees and a few helpers. She said she was doing small things with great love. Soon her sisters were feeding and caring for thousands of people in many countries. Lesson: give Jesus your little loaves, and he will feed many!
2027-04-23.special: Fourth Friday of Resurrection. Latin calendar: St George.
term: Illumination

An ancient name for Baptism (in Greek photismos), used by Justin Martyr and the Fathers. The newly baptised were called the enlightened, because Christ the light had shone on them; this is why a lit candle is given at Baptism.

family.explain: A huge crowd was hungry in a place with no shops. The disciples had only five loaves and two fish. Jesus took them, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them and gave them to the disciples to share. Everyone ate until they were full, and there were twelve baskets left over! Jesus does something even more wonderful at the Holy Qurbana: he gives us himself as the Bread of life.
family.intention: We pray for children who are hungry today, and for all who feed them.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share this week with someone who does not have enough?”

illus: An illustration

A parish in Thrissur began a Friday evening meal for migrant workers and lonely elderly people. On the first evening the volunteers had cooked for forty, and more than seventy came. The young assistant priest stood in the kitchen wondering what to do. An old woman who helped every week said, “Father, do what Jesus did. Say the blessing and start serving.” They served smaller portions, and somehow everyone ate. When the last plate was cleared, there was still rice in the pot. The priest said later that he had read the story of the loaves many times, but that night he understood the line, “You give them something to eat.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Sun of the Resurrection, shine on us now. Fill us with your Spirit, and teach us to give thanks for everything. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you (Ephesians 5:14). Where am I spiritually asleep?
Making the most of the time, because the days are evil (Ephesians 5:16). How do I use my time each day?
Giving thanks to God the Father at all times and for everything (Ephesians 5:20). What am I slow to thank God for?
You give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). Whom is Jesus asking me to feed?
pm.resp: Christ, shine on us and fill us.
interc: For the newly baptised, that the light of Christ may shine in their lives.
For families broken by alcohol and addiction, that they may find healing and the fullness of the Spirit.
For the hungry and for migrant workers far from home, that they may find bread and welcome.
For parish volunteers and all who feed the poor, that the Lord may multiply their gifts.
For ourselves, that we may receive the Holy Qurbana with thanksgiving and share what we have.
pm.close: Father, your Son took the loaves, blessed, broke and gave them, and fed the multitude. Feed us with the Bread of life, fill us with your Spirit, and make us wise, thankful and generous. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Daniel: thrown to the lions for praying to his God, he came out unharmed because he had trusted in God.
Acts: Herod killed James and imprisoned Peter, and the Church prayed fervently for him.
Paul: My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.
Jesus: those who lose their life for my sake will find it.
2027-04-24.action: Pray today for Christians who are persecuted for their faith.
2027-04-24.question: What am I unwilling to lose for Christ?
kidsaint: St George (Geevarghese Sahada)

George was a soldier, brave and strong. When the emperor ordered everyone to give up Jesus, George said no. He was put to death because he loved Jesus more than anything. Later people told a story of George fighting a dragon: it shows that faith in Jesus is stronger than every evil. Lesson: real bravery means staying close to Jesus even when it is hard!
2027-04-24.special: St George, Martyr (Geevarghese Sahada). Fourth Saturday of Resurrection.
term: Sahada

The Syriac word for martyr, literally ‘witness’, like the Greek martyr. St George is called Mar Geevarghese Sahada. A martyr is one who bears witness to Christ by accepting death rather than deny him; the Church honours the martyrs' days as their true birthdays into heaven.

family.explain: Daniel kept praying to God even when the king's law said he must not. So he was thrown into a den full of hungry lions! All night the king could not sleep. In the morning he ran to the den, and Daniel was alive: God had sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths. St George was brave like Daniel: he would not stop loving Jesus, even when soldiers threatened him. Today we celebrate his feast.
family.intention: We pray for children and families in places where it is dangerous to be a Christian.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a time when it is hard for you to say you love Jesus? Let us ask St George to make us brave.”

illus: An illustration

A young woman from Kottayam, a nurse in a hospital abroad, was told by her supervisor that she must stop wearing the small cross she always wore under her collar. She was frightened: her family depended on her salary. That night she remembered the feast of St George at her home parish, and the old priest saying that martyrs were ordinary people who had decided whom they loved most. The next day she went to the supervisor, politely explained what the cross meant to her, and asked whether she could keep it hidden under her uniform. The supervisor agreed. She said later, “It was a small thing. But I learned that I could be weak and faithful at the same time.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you made St George strong in weakness. Gather us now in your presence, and give us his courage and his love for you. Amen. Alleluia!
share: O Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God whom you faithfully serve been able to deliver you from the lions? (Daniel 6:20). When has God delivered me?
While Peter was kept in prison, the church prayed fervently to God for him (Acts 12:5). For whom should our community pray fervently now?
My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness (2 Corinthians 12:9). What weakness of mine can I offer to Christ?
Those who lose their life for my sake will find it (Matthew 10:39). What is Jesus asking me to let go of?
pm.resp: Lord, make us strong in our weakness.
interc: For Christians who are persecuted, imprisoned or threatened for their faith, that the Risen Lord may strengthen and protect them.
For Cardinal Mar George Alencherry, Major Archbishop emeritus, and for all bishops, priests and faithful who bear the name of St George.
For soldiers, police and all who serve in uniform, that they may be just and brave.
For those who are afraid to speak of their faith at work or in college, that they may find courage.
For our families, that we may love Christ first and so love one another more truly.
pm.close: Father, you gave St George the grace to bear witness to your Son even to death. By his intercession, make us faithful witnesses in our own trials, strong in weakness and steadfast in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Jesus refuses every sign but the sign of Jonah: his death and Resurrection on the third day.
Nineveh repented at Jonah's voice; something greater than Jonah is here.
Peter: do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal; if you suffer as a Christian, glorify God for the name.
2027-04-26.action: Make the sign of the Cross openly before a meal today, and pray for persecuted Christians.
2027-04-26.question: Am I still waiting for a sign, when the Risen Lord has already been given to me?

family.explain: Long ago God sent the prophet Jonah to a big city called Nineveh. Jonah was swallowed by a huge fish and after three days he came out again and preached to the city. The people listened, said sorry to God and changed their lives. Jesus said that he would be like Jonah: he would be in the tomb for three days and then rise again. And he did! That is the biggest sign God has given us.
family.intention: We pray for Christians around the world who are laughed at or hurt because they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we need to say sorry to God for, like the people of Nineveh?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Kanjirappally joined a company in Bengaluru and shared a flat with five colleagues. On the first evening he quietly made the sign of the Cross before eating, and the others laughed. For weeks he was ‘the Father’ of the flat. He did not argue and did not stop. Months later, when one of his flatmates lost his mother, it was this young man he knocked on the door of at midnight. ‘You pray,’ he said. ‘Please pray for her.’ They prayed together, and the next morning the friend asked him to explain what Christians believe about the dead. The young man said afterwards that the laughter had been the small price; the midnight knock was the reward.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, you are the sign given to our generation. Open our hearts as we gather in your name. Amen. Alleluia!
share: No sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah (Luke 11:29). What signs or proofs do I still demand of God?
The people of Nineveh repented at the proclamation of Jonah (Luke 11:32). Where is the Lord calling me to change?
Do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal (1 Peter 4:12). What trial am I going through for my faith?
Entrust themselves to a faithful Creator, while continuing to do good (1 Peter 4:19). How can I go on doing good in my difficulty?
pm.resp: Lord, greater than Jonah, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the Risen Christ as the one sign given to the world.
For Christians who suffer for the name of Christ in India and in every land, that they may be strong and joyful.
For those who persecute believers, that their hearts may be turned to peace.
For those who are searching for God and asking for signs, that they may meet the Risen Lord.
For our families, that we may repent and believe like the people of Nineveh.
pm.close: Father, you gave the sign of Jonah when you raised your Son from the heart of the earth. Make us believe without demanding more, repent without delay, and suffer without shame for the name we bear. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: James: be doers of the word, not hearers who look in the mirror and forget.
Pure religion: a bridled tongue, care for orphans and widows, and a life unstained by the world.
Jesus finds a fig tree with only leaves; then he teaches faith that moves mountains.
2027-04-27.action: Visit or call one widow or elderly person living alone this week.
2027-04-27.question: Is my faith all leaves, or is there fruit for the Lord when he comes hungry?

family.explain: Imagine looking in the mirror and seeing your face is dirty, and then walking away without washing it! That is silly, isn't it? St James says that hearing God's word and not doing it is just as silly. God's word is like a mirror: it shows us what to change. Then we have to do it!
family.intention: We pray for children who have no parents, and for grandmothers and grandfathers who live alone.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus asks us to do that we can do together this week?”

illus: An illustration

A parish in the Thrissur area once ran a summer Bible class on the parable of the sheep and the goats. On the last day the teacher, a retired headmistress, did not give a test. She took the twenty children in a hired bus to a home for elderly women run by religious sisters nearby. The children sang the songs they had learned, served tea and sat holding the hands of women who had not had a visitor in months. On the way back a boy of ten said, ‘Teacher, I think that was the exam.’ She told the parents afterwards that it was the best answer any pupil had given her in thirty years.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you speak to us in your word. Let us not only hear it but do it. Come among us now. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Be doers of the word, and not merely hearers (James 1:22). Which word of God have I heard many times but not yet done?
If any think they are religious, and do not bridle their tongues… their religion is worthless (James 1:26). How do I use my tongue at home and on my phone?
To care for orphans and widows in their distress (James 1:27). Whom could I visit this week?
He found nothing at all on it but leaves (Matthew 21:19). Where is my life all show and no fruit?
pm.resp: Lord, make us bear fruit for you.
interc: For the Church, that her preaching may become life in her children.
For orphans, widows and the elderly who live alone, and for all who care for them.
For those who run homes for children, the sick and the old, that they may never lack help.
For children in vacation Bible classes, that they may learn God's word and see it lived.
For our group, that we may pray with faith and bear fruit.
pm.close: Father, you have planted us in the garden of your Church and watered us with the grace of your Son's Resurrection. Do not let us be trees of leaves only, but make us bear the fruit of love, for the glory of your name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Nicodemus comes by night; Jesus tells him he must be born from above, of water and Spirit.
The wind, ruha, blows where it chooses: so is everyone born of the Spirit.
Paul: put to death what is earthly, take off the old self and put on the new, where Christ is all and in all.
2027-04-28.action: Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it today.
2027-04-28.question: Is the new life begun in my Baptism still growing, or have I put the old garment back on?

family.explain: A man called Nicodemus came to see Jesus at night. Jesus told him that to belong to God's kingdom we must be born again, by water and by the Holy Spirit. That happened to us when we were baptised! The Holy Spirit is like the wind: we cannot see it, but we can see what it does.
family.intention: We pray for the children making their First Holy Communion this season, and for all babies who will be baptised.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know the date and the church of each one's Baptism? Let us find out and write it on our calendar.”

illus: An illustration

A father in Pala found his old baptismal certificate while searching for documents for his son's college admission. He sat down at the dining table and read it aloud: the date, the parish, the name of the priest, the names of his godparents, both long dead. His teenage son, who had been impatient to finish the paperwork, asked him what was so interesting about an old certificate. ‘This is the day I was born the second time,’ the father said. That evening the family lit a candle at the prayer corner and renewed their baptismal promises together. The son said nothing then, but a month later, when he left for his hostel, a photocopy of his own baptismal certificate was in his bag.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were raised from the dead, and in Baptism you gave us new birth. Send your Spirit like the wind among us now. Amen. Alleluia!
share: No one can see the kingdom of God without being born from above (John 3:3). What does my Baptism mean to me today?
The wind blows where it chooses (John 3:8). Where have I felt the Spirit at work in my life, unseen but real?
Put to death, therefore, whatever in you is earthly (Colossians 3:5). What earthly thing must die in me this Easter?
Christ is all and in all (Colossians 3:11). Whom do I treat as less than a brother or sister?
pm.resp: Lord, renew in us the grace of our Baptism.
interc: For the Church, the mother who gives birth to children of God from the font.
For the children making their First Holy Communion this season, and for their families.
For catechumens and all who are preparing for Baptism.
For an end to every division of caste, class and race among Christians, and in our land.
For our group, that we may put on the new self each day.
pm.close: Father, through water and the Spirit you have made us your children. Keep us faithful to the grace of our Baptism, clothe us with Christ, and make us one family in him who is all and in all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Hebrews: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts; exhort one another every day.
Jesus: whoever hears my word and believes has passed from death to life; all in the graves will hear his voice.
St Catherine of Siena, an unlettered young woman, became a doctor of the Church and a peacemaker for popes and cities.
2027-04-29.action: Send one message of encouragement in faith today to someone who is drifting.
2027-04-29.question: Is there a word of God I keep putting off until tomorrow?
catechism: The resurrection of all the dead.
St Catherine: everything comes from love.
kidsaint: St Catherine of Siena

Catherine was one of the youngest of more than twenty children in her family! She could not read when she was young, but she loved Jesus so much that she learned, and later she wrote letters to kings and even to the Pope, telling them to make peace and do what God wanted. Lesson: Jesus can use anyone, even a child who does not know much, to do great things!

family.explain: Jesus says that whoever listens to him and believes in God has eternal life, a life that never ends, starting now! And one day, Jesus will call everyone who has died, and they will rise. That is why we pray for Grandpa, Grandma and everyone in our family who has died: they are waiting for Jesus to call them.
family.intention: We pray for all the members of our family who have died, that they may rise to the life of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom shall we remember tonight from our family who has gone to God?”

illus: An illustration

In 1376 St Catherine of Siena travelled to Avignon, where the popes had lived for nearly seventy years, far from Rome. She was twenty-nine, without rank or learning, but she had already written to Pope Gregory XI with astonishing frankness, calling him ‘sweet Christ on earth’ and begging him to return to his see and be a good shepherd. In Avignon she met him in person. Many cardinals opposed the move. In September 1376 Gregory left Avignon, and in January 1377 he entered Rome. Historians still debate how much was due to Catherine, but her letters remain, full of love for the Pope and of courage before him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, today we hear your voice. Soften our hearts and give us life. Through the prayers of St Catherine of Siena, set us on fire with your love. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 3:7–8). Where is my heart becoming hard?
Exhort one another every day, as long as it is called ‘today’ (Hebrews 3:13). Whom can I encourage today?
Anyone who hears my word… has passed from death to life (John 5:24). Do I live as one who already has eternal life?
You have hidden these things from the wise… and revealed them to infants (Matthew 11:25). How does St Catherine's life challenge me?
pm.resp: Lord, give us life.
interc: For the Church, that she may be one, holy and at peace, as St Catherine prayed.
For the Pope and the bishops, that they may be good shepherds, strengthened by the prayers and the honesty of the faithful.
For women in the Church, that their gifts of wisdom and courage may be welcomed and honoured.
For our dead, that they may hear the voice of the Son of God and rise to the resurrection of life.
For those whose hearts are hardened, that today they may hear his voice.
pm.close: Father, your Son has life in himself and gives it to all who believe. Through the prayers of St Catherine of Siena, keep our hearts open to his voice today and every day, and bring us with all our dead to the resurrection of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul came to Corinth in weakness, knowing nothing but Christ crucified, so that faith might rest on God's power.
Jesus: what defiles a person is not what goes into the mouth but what comes out of the heart.
Tomorrow begins the month of May, the month of the Blessed Virgin Mary, model of the clean heart.
2027-04-30.action: Before forwarding any message about a person today, ask: is it true, kind and necessary?
2027-04-30.question: What is in my heart that comes out so easily in my words?

family.explain: Some people thought that eating without washing hands made a person bad before God. Jesus said: what makes us bad is not the food that goes into our mouth, but the bad words and thoughts that come out of our heart. So we need clean hands for eating, but even more we need clean hearts!
family.intention: We pray that our family may speak only kind and true words, and for anyone we have hurt with our words.
family.ask: Ask: “Did any of us say an unkind word today? Shall we say sorry before we sleep?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Kottayam district the mothers' group had a lively phone group of two hundred members. One evening a message arrived about a young woman of the parish, with a blurred photograph and a story that spread in minutes. The group's coordinator, a nurse in her fifties, did not forward it. She phoned the young woman's mother instead, and learned that the story was false from beginning to end. The next morning she wrote in the group: ‘Before we forward anything about a person, let us ask whether we would say it to her face in front of the Blessed Sacrament.’ Several members deleted what they had shared. The coordinator said later that it was the hardest message she had ever sent, and the most necessary.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, crucified and risen, we gather around you. Create in us a clean heart, and let only good words come from our lips tonight. Amen. Alleluia!
share: I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified (1 Corinthians 2:2). What place does the Cross have in my faith during this joyful season?
I came to you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling (1 Corinthians 2:3). Where can God use my weakness?
What comes out of the mouth proceeds from the heart (Matthew 15:18). What do my words this week reveal about my heart?
False witness, slander (Matthew 15:19). Have I passed on anything untrue or unkind about someone?
pm.resp: Lord, create in us a clean heart.
interc: For preachers and catechists, that they may proclaim Christ crucified with the power of the Spirit.
For all who have been harmed by false rumours and slander, that their good name may be restored.
For those who use social media, that their words may build up and not destroy.
For the Jewish people, that God may bless them in his covenant love, and for respect between Christians and Jews.
For our families, that the Marian month may bring us closer to Jesus through his Mother.
pm.close: Father, you revealed your power in the weakness of the Cross and raised your Son in glory. Purify our hearts, guard our tongues, and make our words a witness to Christ crucified and risen. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Puthu Njayar, New Sunday. Christ is risen, and everything is new. In the ancient Church the newly baptised laid aside their white garments today and took their place among the faithful. And for us, children of Mar Thoma, it is the Sunday of our father in faith. Thousands are climbing the hill of Malayattoor today to say with him: My Lord and my God.

On Easter evening the disciples were behind locked doors, afraid. Jesus came through the doors and said: “Peace be with you.” Then he showed them his hands and his side. He is risen in the same body that was nailed to the Cross. The wounds are still there, now shining with glory: the marks of a love that death could not defeat.

Then he breathed on them, as God breathed into Adam, and said: “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them.” On the night of the Resurrection the Lord gave his Church the power to forgive sins. The first gift of Easter is mercy. If you have stayed away from confession for a long time, this Easter season is your time to come home.

Thomas was not there. He said: “Unless I see the mark of the nails… I will not believe.” But notice what he did: he stayed with the community. A week later, on Sunday, he was with them, and Jesus came for him. The Lord did not scold him; he offered him his wounds. And Thomas said the greatest words in the Gospel: “My Lord and my God!” If you have doubts, do not walk away from the Church. Bring them here, on the eighth day. This is where the Lord finds Thomas.

Jesus then speaks to us: “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.” We do not see the wounds. But when the priest lifts up the Host and the Chalice, our grandmothers taught us to whisper Thomas's words. It is not a pious habit only. It is the faith of the Church: the Risen Lord is truly here, Body and Blood.

And faith in the Risen Lord builds a community: “of one heart and soul… There was not a needy person among them.” Our grandparents kept a handful of rice for the poor at every cooking. Let us find our own pidiyari this season: something small, every day, for those in need. And let us go out as Isaiah promised: “For you shall go out in joy, and be led back in peace.” My Lord and my God! Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Thomas said: ‘I will not believe unless I touch Jesus' wounds.’ Then Jesus came and said: ‘Touch them, Thomas, and believe!’
Thomas said: ‘My Lord and my God!’ Mar Thoma is the apostle who, our tradition says, came to Kerala.
When the priest lifts up the Host at Qurbana, you can whisper like Thomas: ‘My Lord and my God!’

homily: Dear friends, today's readings ask: who belongs in God's house? Isaiah speaks to the foreigner who feared he would be shut out, and to the eunuch who called himself a dry tree. God says: I will give them an everlasting name, and my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.

After Easter this came true: one of the very first baptised from beyond Israel was an Ethiopian eunuch reading Isaiah. And we Indians, who received the Gospel through Saint Thomas, are the foreigners God brought to his holy mountain. In the Church no one is a stranger.

In Jerusalem the apostles are on trial. Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee and teacher of the law, gives wise counsel: if this is of human origin it will fail; but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow it. Two thousand years have proved him right. The apostles are flogged, and they go out rejoicing, and every day, in the temple and at home, they proclaim Jesus as the Messiah.

Paul blesses God for every spiritual blessing: we were chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world, adopted as children, redeemed by his blood, and sealed with the Holy Spirit, the pledge of our inheritance. Our Qurbana, with the ancient Anaphora of Mar Addai and Mar Mari, sings this same blessing.

In the Gospel our own father in faith, Saint Thomas, asks: Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way? Jesus answers: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. He gives Thomas not a map but himself. And whoever has seen Jesus has seen the Father.

Thomas followed that Way all the way to India. This week, let us follow it too: welcome the stranger, trust God's work, bless the Father each morning, and bring our honest questions to Jesus. He is the way home. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Saint Thomas once said to Jesus, ‘We don't know the way!’ And Jesus said, ‘I am the way!’ If we follow Jesus, we will always get home to God.
Saint Thomas came all the way to India to tell our ancestors about Jesus. Let us thank God for him today!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Zion in exile said: the LORD has forsaken me, my Lord has forgotten me. And God answered: can a woman forget her nursing child? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you. See, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands (Isaiah 49:15–16). On Easter evening the Risen Lord showed his disciples his hands. Our names are written there.

Isaiah says that Zion, who thought she was barren, will find her house too crowded with children. That is the Church, our mother. Today, the World Prayer Day for Vocations, we thank God for the priests, sisters and missionaries he has given us, and we ask him for more.

In Acts, Peter and John lay their hands on the new believers of Samaria, and they receive the Holy Spirit. Then Simon the magician offers money for that power. Peter says: may your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain God's gift with money! A vocation is not a career to buy, nor a family honour to collect. It is a gift and a call, freely received and freely given.

Paul tells us that we were dead in our sins. But God, who is rich in mercy, made us alive together with Christ. By grace we have been saved. Every vocation, and every Christian life, begins with that gift.

In the Gospel Jesus says: you will have pain, but your pain will turn into joy. Like a mother in labour, who forgets the pain when her child is born. Mary stood by the Cross in that hour, and on Easter morning her sorrow was turned into joy. Jesus promises us: no one will take your joy from you.

So today let us ask, as he told us to ask. Let us pray every day for vocations from our families. Parents, do not be afraid if God calls your son or daughter. Young people, listen; he may be calling you. And all of us, let us bring our sorrows to him, and let him turn them into joy. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, God says: even if a mother forgot her baby, I will never forget you. Your name is written on God's hands! You are never alone.
Today we pray for priests and sisters. Maybe Jesus is calling you to be one of them one day! Say a little prayer: Jesus, what do you want me to be?

homily: Dear friends, this Fifth Sunday of Resurrection bears the name of Mar Addai, the apostle of Edessa. When our priest prays the Anaphora of Mar Addai and Mar Mari, he prays with one of the oldest Eucharistic prayers in the world. Eusebius records a tradition that it was the apostle Thomas, our father in faith, who sent Thaddeus, known in Syriac tradition as Addai, to Edessa.

Isaiah sings of the Servant despised by all, whom kings will one day honour. God gives him as a covenant, to say to prisoners, “Come out.” “Sing for joy, O heavens, and exult, O earth.” The despised Servant exalted is Christ, rejected on the Cross and risen at Easter.

In Acts, a prisoner of darkness is called out: Saul, breathing threats against the disciples. A light flashes, he falls, and hears, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.” Christ is one with his Church. Blind for three days, Saul is then baptised and becomes the great apostle.

Hebrews says that through the blood of Jesus a new and living way is open to us: “let us approach with a true heart.” And it adds: let us not neglect to meet together, but encourage one another. Even then, some stayed away on Sunday. We need one another, and we need the altar.

In the Gospel the disciples fish all night and catch nothing. At daybreak Jesus fills their nets. The beloved disciple cries, “It is the Lord!” On the shore Jesus has a fire, fish and bread ready, and he says, “Come and have breakfast.” He takes the bread and gives it to them.

Among them is Thomas, who would bring the Gospel to our shores. Every Sunday the Risen Lord stands on the shore of our tired week, fills our empty nets with grace, and says at the altar: Come and eat. Let us recognise him, and bring someone back with us next Sunday. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, the disciples fished all night and caught nothing. Then Jesus told them where to throw the net, and it was full! And Jesus cooked them breakfast on the beach!
Every Sunday at the Holy Qurbana, Jesus says to us, ‘Come and eat.’ Let us say like John: ‘It is the Lord!’

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah sings to a woman with an empty house: “Sing, O barren one… Enlarge the site of your tent.” This week the Church is that woman. On Good Friday she was a few women and one disciple at the Cross. On Easter night the font gave her new children. Now God says: make room, there are more coming.

And God adds a promise: “For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you… my steadfast love shall not depart from you.” If you have been through a dark time, hear this: it was a brief moment. His love has not moved.

But a bigger family brings bigger problems. In Acts the Greek-speaking widows are being forgotten at the daily meal. The apostles listen. They do not say, ‘Stop complaining.’ They ask the community to choose seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom, and they lay hands on them. These are the first deacons. And the word of God spreads even faster.

Paul tells us where the strength comes from. In Baptism we were buried with Christ and raised with him. God erased the record that stood against us, “nailing it to the cross.” The powers that held us are disarmed. We do not serve out of fear. We serve as children of God, no longer slaves.

Then Jesus sends the Twelve, Thomas among them, with nothing in their bags. “You received without payment; give without payment.” Everything we have from God is a gift: our life, our faith, the Holy Qurbana we receive every Sunday. Nobody paid for it.

So this week let us give something without payment. Visit one widow. Do one job with no thanks. Pray for our deacons and seminarians. A Church that gives freely is the best sermon on the Resurrection. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told his friends: ‘You got it as a gift, so give it as a gift!’ God gives us so many presents: our family, our food, his love.
This week, give a present of kindness: help someone without being asked, and do not ask for anything back.

homily: Dear friends, on the first Friday after Easter the Church of the East remembers all the saints and above all the martyrs. They belong in Easter week, because they went with Christ through death into life. Our tradition remembers Mar Shemun bar Sabbae and the martyrs of Persia, killed, the story says, on a Good Friday long ago. And our own Church has given witnesses in our own time, like Blessed Rani Maria, whose family forgave the man who killed her.

In Daniel three young men face the furnace and say: our God is able to save us; but if not, we will still not bow down. That ‘but if not’ is the heart of faith. We do not love God only for what he gives. And in the fire they walk and sing, and a fourth man walks with them. Christ does not always take us out of the fire, but he never leaves us alone in it.

Stephen, full of grace and power, is dragged before the council on false charges. Stephen was a Jew, like the apostles; this is not a story against any people. It is the story of a witness whose face shines like an angel's, who sees heaven open and prays for those who stone him. He died as his Master died: forgiving.

Hebrews reminds us of the long line of witnesses. Abel, of whom it is written, “he died, but through his faith he still speaks.” Abraham, who “set out, not knowing where he was going.” They lived for a city they did not yet see. So did the martyrs. So must we.

Jesus says three times: Do not be afraid. Your Father sees every sparrow, and he has counted the hairs of your head. And then: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.” Most of us will not be asked to die. But every day we are asked to acknowledge him: at work, in college, in the family chat, in how we treat the poor.

Today is also First Friday. Let us go to the Heart of Jesus, pierced and risen, and ask for a little of the martyrs' courage. And before tonight let us make one small act of witness. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember the martyrs. They were brave friends of Jesus who would not stop loving him, even when they were hurt.
Jesus says: ‘Do not be afraid! God counts every hair on your head.’ Let us be brave and say: ‘I love Jesus!’

opts.a: The whole family of the saints
intro: In our Church the first Friday after Easter is the feast of the martyrs and of all the saints. It is a family feast: the Church in heaven and the Church on earth together.

sub: The souls of the righteous are in God's hand.
points.apply: Learn the life of one saint this Easter season.

points.h: The saints of our own soil
sub: Let us now praise famous men.
points.apply: Pray at the tomb or shrine of a saint of our Church, or ask their intercession at home.

sub: Chosen before the foundation of the world.
points.apply: Choose one practical step toward holiness this week.

concl: We are surrounded by a family of witnesses who pray for us.
Their feast is our call: we too are called to be saints.
opts.resolve: This Easter season I will learn the life of one saint and take one practical step toward holiness.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in the joy of Easter our Church keeps the feast of the martyrs and of all the saints. Why now? Because the saints are the fruit of Easter. Christ's victory over death is seen first in those who followed him through death into life.

The Book of Wisdom says: the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will ever touch them (Wisdom 3:1). Hebrews tells us that we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses (Hebrews 12:1). We do not run the race alone. The saints are not far from us. They are our elder brothers and sisters, cheering us on and praying for us.

Sirach says: let us now sing the praises of famous men, our ancestors in their generations (Sirach 44:1). Our Church has its own family of saints: St Alphonsa, St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, St Euphrasia, St Mariam Thresia, Blessed Rani Maria and many others. Hebrews says: remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7).

But this feast is not only about them. God said to Israel: you shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy (Leviticus 19:2). Paul says God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love (Ephesians 1:4). Holiness is not for a few special people. It is the vocation of every baptised person, in the kitchen, the office and the field.

So let us thank God today for the saints, especially the martyrs. Let us learn the life of one saint this season. And let us take one practical step toward holiness, so that one day we may join them in the great feast of heaven, of which every Holy Qurbana is a foretaste. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.

intro: Stephen, the first martyr, died praying for his killers. At his feet lay the coats of the witnesses, and a young man named Saul was watching. The blood of martyrs is the seed of the Church.

points.h: False witnesses and the true witness
points.apply: Refuse to join in gossip or false accusation this week.

points.h: Lord, do not hold this sin against them
points.apply: Pray daily this week for someone who has hurt you.

sub: The grain of wheat that dies.
points.apply: Pray for Christians persecuted today, and support them in some practical way.

concl: The martyr's strongest word is forgiveness.
God makes the blood of witnesses the seed of new life.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray for one who has hurt me and for persecuted Christians.
homily: Dear friends, in today's reading Stephen, full of grace and power, is accused by false witnesses who say he speaks against the holy place and the law (Acts 6:13). The Psalm had prayed: false witnesses have risen against me (Psalm 27:12). The world has often answered the truth with lies.

The word martyr means witness. Stephen bore witness not only with his words but with his face: all who sat in the council saw that his face was like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). Later, as they were stoning him, he knelt down and cried out: Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:60).

In the Old Testament, the priest Zechariah was also stoned in the court of the Lord's house, and as he died he said: may the LORD see and avenge! (2 Chronicles 24:22). Stephen prays differently, because he has learned from Jesus on the Cross. The martyr's greatest victory is not to die bravely, but to die forgiving.

And here is the surprise. The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul, and Saul approved of their killing him (Acts 7:58; 8:1). Stephen's prayer was answered in that very man, who became the Apostle Paul. Jesus had said: unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit (John 12:24). That day the Church was scattered, and the word spread everywhere.

Today many Christians still suffer for their faith. Let us pray for them and help them. Let us refuse to join in false accusations. And let us pray every day this week for someone who has hurt us, as Stephen did. Then we too will be witnesses of the risen Lord. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.

Dear friends, three women walk to the tomb at sunrise with spices and one worry: “Who will roll away the stone for us?” It was a real worry; the stone was very large. But when they looked up, it had already been rolled back.

How often we are like them. We worry for weeks about a conversation, a confession, a reconciliation, and when we finally go, God has already gone ahead and moved the stone. Easter teaches us to walk towards the stone.

The angel says: “He has been raised; he is not here. Look, there is the place they laid him.” The tomb is empty because the Lord is risen in his body. He is not a memory. He is alive, and we meet him at this altar.

Then: “go, tell his disciples and Peter.” Why Peter? Because Peter had denied him. The Lord did not want Peter to think he was finished. If you have failed, put your own name there: tell the disciples, and tell me.

Paul adds: “seek the things that are above… for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.” The newly baptised will take off their white garments, but their new life goes on, hidden. So does ours: in quiet prayers, faithful work, patient love. None of it is lost; it will be revealed with him in glory.
Tomorrow is New Sunday, the Sunday of Mar Thoma. Today let us take one step towards our stone, and lift up our minds to the Lord. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, the women were worried: ‘Who will move the big stone?’ But God had already moved it, and Jesus was risen!
When you are worried, tell Jesus. He is already there to help you.

homily: Dear friends, the Easter octave is over and we are back to ordinary Mondays. Today's readings show what Easter looks like in ordinary life: in a parish with quarrels, and on a road walked by two tired disciples.

Paul hears that the Corinthians are divided: I belong to Paul, I belong to Apollos, I belong to Cephas. He asks: Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? There is only one Lord who died for us, and only one name in which we were baptised.
We have our own versions of this: my priest, my group, my side of the family. Paul says: look at the Cross. When we look together at the Crucified and Risen Lord, our little parties lose their power.
In the Gospel two disciples walk to Emmaus with a stranger. At the village he seems to go on, and they beg him: Stay with us, because it is almost evening. The Lord waits to be invited.

At table he took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them, and their eyes were opened. They knew him in the breaking of the bread, as we know him at every Holy Qurbana. And that same hour they ran back to Jerusalem to the gathered community.
This week, let us invite him every evening: Lord, stay with us. And let us bring one quarrel to his table, so that he may make us one. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, two friends of Jesus did not recognise him on the road. But when he broke the bread at supper, they knew him! At Holy Qurbana, when the priest breaks the Holy Bread, Jesus is there for us too.
Tonight, before you sleep, say a little prayer: ‘Jesus, stay with us!’

homily: Dear friends, a few days earlier Saul had come to Damascus to arrest Christians. Then the Risen Lord met him, and he was baptised. Today we hear: immediately he began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, saying, He is the Son of God.
No long delay, no waiting to become respectable. The man who came to silence the name now cannot stop speaking it. Easter raises dead hearts as well as dead bodies.

Then danger came, and his new brothers lowered him down the city wall in a basket at night. The great apostle began his work being carried. The Risen Lord often makes us strong by first making us small, and by teaching us to lean on one another.
In the Gospel Jesus says: How can you believe when you accept glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from God? Faith dies where we live for applause.

And he says: If you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me. The Old Testament is the word of God, and it speaks of Christ. That is why at the Holy Qurbana we hear the Law and the Prophets before the Gospel.
This week, let us speak the name of Jesus without fear, let ourselves be carried by the prayer of others, and seek only the glory that comes from God. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Saul used to be against Jesus. But when he met Jesus he changed completely and told everyone, ‘Jesus is the Son of God!’ His friends even saved him by lowering him down a wall in a basket!
Jesus can change any heart. Let us pray for someone who does not know Jesus yet.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes to the Galatians with a battle-cry: For freedom Christ has set us free. Stand firm, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.

Some teachers had told these Gentile Christians that faith in Christ was not enough. Paul says: if you try to earn salvation, you cut yourselves off from grace. The Risen Lord who broke the chains of death does not give us new chains.
But Christian freedom is not doing whatever we like. Paul says: the only thing that counts is faith working through love. Faith that does not love is dead. Faith that loves lives in true freedom.
In the Gospel people bring a deaf man to Jesus. Jesus takes him aside, touches his ears and tongue, looks up to heaven, sighs and says: Ephphatha, Be opened. At once he hears and speaks.
The Lord still heals us through signs he can touch us with: water, oil, bread and wine. In every sacrament he says over us, Ephphatha. And the people cry: He has done everything well.
Today, let us ask him to open our ears to his word and our lips to praise him and to speak kindly. And let our faith work through love. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus met a man who could not hear. Jesus touched his ears and said, ‘Ephphatha!’ which means ‘Be opened!’ And the man could hear!
Let us ask Jesus to open our ears to listen to God and to our parents, and our mouths to say kind words.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes from prison, not knowing if he will live. He does not ask the Philippians to get him out. He asks: live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ.

Our daily behaviour is the visible face of the Gospel. And Paul says something surprising: God has granted you the privilege not only of believing in Christ, but of suffering for him. After Easter the Cross remains, but it has a new meaning. Those who suffer with the Risen Lord share his victory.
In the Gospel a Canaanite woman, a complete outsider, cries out: Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon. Jesus does not answer. The disciples want her sent away.
But she kneels and says: Lord, help me. When Jesus speaks of the children's bread, she answers: Yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table. She will not give up.

Jesus says: Woman, great is your faith! And her daughter is healed. His silence drew out a greater faith. And now, at the Holy Qurbana, the children's bread is given to all who come in faith, from every nation.
If you have been praying a long time for a child or for someone you love, stand beside this mother. God's silence is not his absence. Keep kneeling. Keep saying: Lord, help me. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, a mother came to Jesus because her little girl was sick. Jesus did not answer at first, but she kept asking: ‘Lord, help me!’ And Jesus healed her daughter.
When you pray and nothing seems to happen, don't stop! Keep saying: ‘Jesus, help me.’ He always hears you.

homily: Dear friends, every Friday is a little Good Friday, even in the Easter season. Today Paul says: For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
In Corinth people admired clever speakers. Paul preached a Saviour who died on a cross. It sounded absurd. But God chose the foolishness of the Cross to save those who believe.

Some want signs on demand; some want wisdom they can control. We proclaim Christ crucified, the power of God and the wisdom of God. And because he is risen, the Cross is no longer a sign of defeat. Our Mar Thoma Cross flowers at its ends: the tree of death has become the tree of life.
In the Gospel Jesus tells of a sower who throws seed everywhere: on the path, on rock, among thorns, and on good soil. Much seems wasted, yet the good soil yields thirty, sixty, a hundredfold.

Jesus is the sower, and his word is the seed. The Cross itself looked like a seed thrown away, but it rose in the Easter harvest. The question is about us: what kind of ground does his word find in me?
This week, let us clear away one thorn, and let the word take root. Let anyone with ears to hear listen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about a farmer who threw seeds. Some were eaten by birds, some dried up, some got choked by thorns, but some grew into a big harvest!
God's word is like a seed. When you listen to Bible stories and remember them, the seed grows in your heart.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Colossians: Above all, clothe yourselves with love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony. Love is the belt that holds all the other virtues in place.
He gives three gifts for a Christian home: let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts; let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; and sing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs to God with gratitude.

When a Kerala family lights the lamp at dusk and gathers to pray, read the Gospel and sing, that is Colossians 3 lived out. And Paul adds: whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks. Our whole life can become a Qurbana, an offering with thanks.

In the Gospel the Risen Lord stands among his disciples and says, Peace be with you. They think he is a ghost. He says: Look at my hands and my feet; touch me and see; a ghost does not have flesh and bones. And he eats a piece of fish before them.
Our faith is not in a ghost or an idea. Jesus is risen in his own body, glorified, still bearing his wounds. And the same Lord gives us his true Body and Blood at the altar.
Tonight, let us light the lamp, pray and sing together at home, and let his peace rule in our hearts. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus came back to his friends after he rose, they thought he was a ghost! But he said, ‘Touch me! Look at my hands!’ And he ate some fish. Jesus is really alive!
Tonight at family prayer, sing a happy hymn to Jesus, because he is risen.

homily: Dear friends, St James says: be patient until the coming of the Lord. Look at the farmer. After he sows, he waits for the early and the late rains (James 5:7). He cannot hurry the clouds, but he does not sit idle either. He watches, he weeds, he keeps the field ready.

That is how a Christian waits in the Easter season. Christ is risen; he will come again. While we wait, James warns us: do not grumble against one another. Impatient people turn on each other. Let us strengthen our hearts instead, and let our yes be yes and our no be no.

In the Gospel Jesus tells of ten bridesmaids. All ten were invited, all had lamps, and all fell asleep while the bridegroom was delayed. The difference was the oil. Five had brought it; five had not. And when the cry came at midnight, the foolish could not borrow it.

Some things cannot be borrowed. No one can lend you faith, love or a life of prayer at the last minute. That oil we gather day by day: in prayer, in the Holy Qurbana, in confession, in kindness to the poor.

The Bridegroom has already come back from the grave, and his feast has begun at our altar. Let us keep the lamp lit at our Baptism burning, so that whenever he knocks, we are ready to go in with him. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about girls with lamps waiting for a wedding. The wise ones brought extra oil. Your prayers and your kind acts are oil for the lamp in your heart!
Tonight, when the family prays, look at the lamp or candle and say: ‘Jesus, keep my heart shining for you!’

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes to a very young church in Thessalonica, and he begins with those who serve it. Respect those who labour among you, he says, and esteem them very highly in love because of their work (1 Thessalonians 5:12–13). Think of your priest, the sisters, the catechism teachers, the sacristan who opens the church before dawn. Let us thank them.

Then Paul gives us the Easter life in three short lines: rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances. He wrote this to people who were suffering. Our joy does not depend on how the day goes. It depends on the fact that Christ is risen, and that never changes.
And he adds: do not quench the Spirit. The Spirit is a fire. Neglect and fear can smother it. As we move toward Pentecost, let us keep that fire burning by prayer.

In the Gospel Jesus explains the sower. The seed is always good; the soil makes the difference. The hard path, where the word never enters. The rocky ground, where joy has no root. The thorns, where worries and money choke the word. And the good soil, which bears fruit a hundredfold.

Every heart has a little of each. This week, let us break up the hard path with prayer, let our Easter joy put down roots, and pull out the thorns of worry by giving thanks in all things. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says your heart is like a garden and his word is a seed. Be good soil: listen to Jesus, pray every day, and you will grow beautiful fruit!
St Paul says: rejoice always, pray always, say thank you always. Tonight, before you sleep, tell Jesus three things you are thankful for.

homily: Dear friends, Paul is in prison. He does not know whether he will live or die. And he writes: for me, living is Christ and dying is gain (Philippians 1:21). If my life is money, death is loss. If my life is Christ, death brings me closer to him.

Paul is torn. He would like to depart and be with Christ, which is far better. But he knows his people still need him, so he is ready to stay and work for their progress and joy in faith. That is Easter faith: no fear of death, and great love for this life as a time of service.

In the Gospel a leper kneels before Jesus. Lepers had to live alone, outside the village. He says: Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean. He does not doubt the power of Jesus; he only asks whether Jesus wants to.

And Jesus stretches out his hand and touches him. I do choose. Be made clean! The touch that should have made Jesus unclean makes the leper clean. Then Jesus sends him to the priest, so that he can return to his people and to worship.

The Risen Lord still stretches out his hand, in Confession, in the Anointing of the Sick, and in Holy Qurbana. Let us bring him what we hide. And let us be his hand for someone whom everyone else avoids. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, a sick man asked Jesus: do you want to make me well? Jesus touched him and said: yes, I want to! Jesus always wants to help us. Tell him what makes you sad.
Is there a child in your class whom nobody plays with? Be like Jesus: go and say hello first!

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Corinthians about the churches of Macedonia. They were poor and suffering, yet their joy overflowed in generosity.
