They gave beyond their means, and they begged to share in helping the poor of Jerusalem. Why? Because they first gave themselves to the Lord (2 Corinthians 8:5).
Our grandmothers knew this. Every day they set aside a handful of rice for the church and the poor, even when there was little in the house. That is Macedonian generosity in a Kerala kitchen.

And Paul reminds us why we give: Jesus Christ was rich, yet for our sake he became poor, so that by his poverty we might become rich (2 Corinthians 8:9). He gave everything, even his life. Every gift we make is a small echo of his.

In the Gospel a storm hits the boat. Jesus is asleep on a cushion. The disciples shout: Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? He rises, rebukes the wind, and says to the sea: Peace! Be still! And there is a great calm.

Then he asks them, and us: why are you afraid? He was in the boat all the time. He slept in the tomb and rose again; he is in the boat of his Church today. When storms come, let us wake him with our prayer, and let us not allow fear to close our hands to the poor. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus was sleeping in a boat when a storm came. When his friends called him, he said to the waves: be still! And they obeyed. When you are scared at night, say: Jesus, you are here with me.
Grandmothers in Kerala used to save a handful of rice every day for poor people. Can you save one coin or one sweet this week to share?

homily: Dear friends, in Rome some Christians ate everything and others did not. Each side despised the other. Paul says: we who are strong ought to put up with the failings of the weak, and not to please ourselves (Romans 15:1). The test of my freedom is whether it builds up my neighbour.

Why? Because Christ did not please himself. He carried the insults meant for us all the way to the Cross. Today is Friday, the day of the Cross. To bear with a weak brother or sister is to stand a little under that Cross with him.

And Paul prays that God may grant us to live in harmony, so that together we may glorify God with one voice. Families, parishes and even Churches need this prayer. Let us pray it today, and let us take the first step toward someone with whom we disagree.

In the Gospel Jesus sees a man with a withered right hand, the hand he needed for work. On the sabbath some watch to accuse him. Jesus brings the man into the middle and asks: is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to destroy it?

Then he says: stretch out your hand. The man obeys, and he is healed. Sunday, the day of the Resurrection, is our Lord's Day. Let us keep it holy at the Qurbana, and then by doing good: visiting the sick, helping the poor, making peace. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a man who could not move his hand: stretch it out! The man tried, and Jesus healed him. When something seems too hard, try with Jesus!
Sunday is Jesus' special day. Go to Holy Qurbana, and then do something kind for someone, like visiting grandparents!

homily: Dear friends, St James asks: what good is it if you say you have faith but do not have works? He imagines a brother or sister without clothes or food, and someone says: go in peace; keep warm and eat your fill. Kind words, but the hungry person is still hungry. So faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead (James 2:17).

This does not mean we earn heaven by our deeds. Faith is God's gift. But living faith works through love, as a living tree bears fruit. At the end of every Qurbana we are sent in peace. That is not a goodbye; it is a mission to feed and serve.

In the Gospel Jesus asks: why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do what I tell you? Then he tells of two builders. One dug deeply and laid the foundation on rock. The other built on the ground without a foundation. When the flood came, the first house stood, and the second fell with a great crash.

In the dry season the two houses looked the same. Only the flood showed the difference. Every life will meet floods. What matters is what lies underneath. The rock is Christ, the stone the builders rejected, whom God raised at Easter.
Today is Saturday, and we remember the Blessed Virgin Mary, who heard the word of God and did it. Let us ask her to help us dig deep: to hear Jesus and to act. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told of a house built on rock. When the flood came, it did not fall! When you listen to Jesus and obey him, you are building on rock.
Don't just say ‘I will help’. Help! Today, do one helpful thing at home without being asked.

homily: Dear friends, on this Monday of the fourth week of Easter, Paul gives Timothy a solemn charge, and Jesus tells a story that is hard to forget.

Paul calls two witnesses: the God who gives life to all things, and Christ Jesus, who made the good confession before Pilate. Jesus stood bound and alone, and spoke the truth calmly. Timothy made his own good confession at his Baptism. So did we. Paul's charge is for us too: keep that confession clean until the Lord comes.

Then Paul sings: God is “the King of kings and Lord of lords”, who “dwells in unapproachable light”. No one can see him. And yet in the Risen Christ that light has come near: the disciples touched him and ate with him. In the Holy Qurbana we bow before the hidden majesty of God, and we receive the Lord himself.

In the Gospel the owner of the vineyard sends servant after servant, and at last he says: “I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.” They kill him. Jesus told this story days before he was led outside the city to die. It was a warning to those who plotted against him; it is a mirror for us.
Today we are the tenants. The vineyard is the Church. God still asks for fruit: faith, mercy, justice. And God has answered the tenants with Easter: the rejected stone has become the cornerstone.
So let us ask ourselves today: what fruit will the Owner find in my part of the vineyard? Let us give him a good share this week. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about a vineyard. The owner sent his own dear son, but the farmers did not welcome him. Jesus was talking about himself!
God has given us his vineyard, the Church, to look after. Every kind thing you do is a sweet grape for God!

homily: Dear friends, today Paul speaks to the rich, and Jesus speaks about camels and needles. Both are speaking about where we put our hope.

Paul does not say that riches are evil. He says: do not be proud, and do not set your hopes “on the uncertainty of riches, but rather on God who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment.” Then he gives a plan: do good, be rich in good works, be generous and ready to share, and so take hold of “the life that really is life.” That life is the life of the Risen Christ.

Paul also tells Timothy: “guard what has been entrusted to you.” The faith is a deposit placed in our hands. We do not own it or change it; we keep it by living it and handing it on whole to our children.

In the Gospel Jesus says it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom. The disciples ask, “Then who can be saved?” And Jesus looks at them and says: “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.”

No one saves himself. God can release a heart tied to its possessions, just as he raised his Son from the tomb. And he promises a hundredfold to those who leave things for his sake, and a share in the renewal of all things.
So today let us move our hope from what we own to the God who gives. Let us give something away before we buy something for ourselves. For God, all things are possible. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said a camel could go through the hole of a needle more easily than a rich person could get into heaven. That is impossible! But Jesus said: for God, everything is possible.
God can make our hearts kind and generous. Today, share something you like with someone else!

homily: Dear friends, today the Letter to the Hebrews takes us back to a mysterious king who met Abraham with bread and wine.

Melchizedek, king of Salem, “brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.” His name means king of righteousness; Salem means peace. Scripture tells us nothing of his birth or death, so Hebrews says he resembles the Son of God and remains a priest forever. He is a picture of Christ.

Hebrews then says something full of Easter joy: the old priests were mortal, but Christ is “one of whom it is testified that he lives.” He holds his priesthood for ever, and “he always lives to make intercession” for us. Right now, the Risen Lord is praying for you before the Father.
And in every Holy Qurbana, the eternal Priest offers himself under the signs of bread and wine, as Melchizedek once foreshadowed. Our priests stand at the altar in his name.

In the Gospel Jesus calls his witnesses: John the Baptist, “a burning and shining lamp”; the works the Father gave him to do; and the Father himself. At Easter the Father gave his greatest testimony: he raised his Son from the dead.
Now it is our turn to be witnesses. Let us pray today for our priests, lean on Christ's intercession when we cannot pray, and let our works point to him. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, long ago a king called Melchizedek brought bread and wine to Abraham and blessed him. He was a picture of Jesus, our priest for ever!
Jesus is alive and he prays for you every day. Tonight, say thank you to Jesus for praying for you!

homily: Dear friends, today Peter warns us about false teachers, and Jesus warns us about worship that stays on the lips.

Peter says false teachers will come, bringing in destructive opinions secretly, and “They will even deny the Master who bought them.” Christ bought us with his own Blood. A teaching that empties the Cross or the Resurrection denies the very Lord who bought us.

How do we know true teaching? The Church answers: by the faith of the apostles, handed down in Scripture and Tradition and taught by the bishops in communion with Peter's successor. Our forefathers in Kerala kept the faith of St Thomas for centuries by asking: is this what our fathers received?

In the Gospel Jesus sees some who used a religious vow to avoid supporting their parents. He says: “for the sake of your tradition, you make void the word of God.” And he quotes Isaiah: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.”
This word is for us first. We can keep every fast and feast and still neglect our parents or speak bitterly of a neighbour. Jesus wants our hearts, not only our lips.
So today, let us test the voices we listen to, look at the crucifix and remember the price, and do one real act of love for our parents. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said some people said nice prayers with their mouths, but their hearts were far from God. God wants our hearts too!
Today, show love at home with your hands and your heart: help Amma or Appa without being asked!

homily: Dear friends, today Paul gives us a little hymn, and Mark gives us the feeding of the five thousand.

The hymn says: “Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.” The first Christians probably sang it at Baptism. We were asleep, we were dead, and the Risen Christ has shone on us. That is why Baptism is called illumination, and why we receive a lit candle.

Then Paul says: be careful how you live; make the most of the time; do not get drunk, but be filled with the Spirit, singing psalms and hymns and “giving thanks to God the Father at all times and for everything.” A Spirit-filled home is a singing and thankful home.

In the Gospel, the crowd is hungry and the place is deserted. Jesus says to the disciples: “You give them something to eat.” They have only five loaves and two fish. He takes them, blesses, breaks and gives them through the disciples, and all are filled, with twelve baskets left over.
These are the actions of every Holy Qurbana. The Risen Lord still feeds his people with his own Body, and he still asks us to bring our small loaves and to share them with the hungry.
So today, let us wake up to Christ's light, give thanks for everything, and bring our little gifts to him. He will make them enough. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus fed five thousand people with five loaves and two fish! He took the bread, said thank you to God, broke it and shared it.
At the Holy Qurbana Jesus gives us the best bread of all: himself. Today, share something with a friend, like Jesus did!

homily: Dear friends, today we keep the feast of Mar Geevarghese Sahada, St George the Martyr, whose name is carried by so many of our families and churches.

History tells us little, but enough: George was a soldier who refused to deny Christ in the persecution under Diocletian, and he was put to death, probably at the beginning of the fourth century. His tomb at Lydda was honoured by pilgrims. The dragon story came later; it is a legend that shows the victory of faith over evil.

Daniel too chose God above the king's law. Thrown to the lions, he was found alive at dawn, “because he had trusted in his God.” A sealed stone, a long night, a dawn visit, and the servant of God alive: it sounds like Easter.

In Acts, Herod kills James and imprisons Peter, and “the church prayed fervently to God for him.” The Church has always carried its martyrs and prisoners in prayer. Let us do the same today for Christians who suffer for their faith.

Paul reveals the secret of courage. He begged God to take away his thorn, and heard: “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” Martyrs are not people without fear; they are weak people in whom the power of Christ lives.

Jesus says: “those who lose their life for my sake will find it.” Most of us will not be asked to die, but we are asked every day to lose a little life for him. Let us ask St George to make us brave, and pray for all who bear his name. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, St George was a brave soldier who loved Jesus more than anything. He would not give up Jesus, even when he was threatened.
You can be brave like St George: say your prayers, tell the truth, and be kind even when it is hard!

homily: Dear friends, the crowds around Jesus wanted a sign, a great proof from heaven. Jesus said: no sign will be given to this generation except the sign of Jonah (Luke 11:29).

Jonah was three days in the belly of the great fish, and then came out and preached. Jesus was three days in the heart of the earth, and then rose. We are in the season of the Resurrection: the sign has been given. The tomb is empty.

The people of Nineveh, a pagan city, repented at the preaching of Jonah. The queen of the South came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon. And Jesus says: something greater than Jonah is here, something greater than Solomon is here (Luke 11:31–32). Our Church remembers Nineveh every year in the Moonnu Nombu. In this Easter season, let the Risen Lord change us as Jonah's voice changed Nineveh.

Peter tells the first Christians not to be surprised at the fiery ordeal. If you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but glorify God because you bear this name (1 Peter 4:12, 16). Rejoice that you share the sufferings of Christ, for you will also share his glory.

When trouble comes for our faith, let us do what Peter says: entrust ourselves to the faithful Creator and keep on doing good (1 Peter 4:19). That is the sign of Jonah lived in our own life. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, do you know the story of Jonah? He was inside a big fish for three days, and then he came out! Jesus said he would be like Jonah: three days in the tomb, and then he would rise. And he did! When you see a picture of Jonah and the fish, remember: Jesus is alive!

homily: Dear friends, St James gives us a picture: someone looks in a mirror, sees his face, walks away and forgets what he looks like (James 1:23–24). That, he says, is a person who hears the word and does not do it. The word of God is a mirror; it is given to change us.

Then James tells us what pure religion is: to bridle the tongue, to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep ourselves unstained by the world (James 1:26–27). Not only long prayers, but a guarded tongue and open hands.
In the Gospel Jesus comes to a fig tree, hungry, and finds nothing on it but leaves. The tree withers. Leaves without fruit: that is what a life of hearing without doing looks like.

But Jesus does not stop at the warning. He tells his disciples: if you have faith and do not doubt, you can say to this mountain, be lifted up and thrown into the sea, and it will be done; whatever you ask for in prayer with faith, you will receive (Matthew 21:21–22). The Risen Lord gives us the grace to bear fruit, if we ask.
This week, let us do one word we have heard, and visit one person who is alone. Let the Lord find fruit on our branches. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus came to a tree looking for fruit, but it had only leaves. Jesus wants our lives to have fruit: kind words, helping hands, saying sorry. Today, can you do one kind thing at home without being asked? That is fruit for Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, Nicodemus, a respected teacher, comes to Jesus by night. Jesus tells him: no one can see the kingdom of God without being born from above (John 3:3). Nicodemus asks: how can an old man be born again?

Jesus answers: no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit (John 3:5). This is what happened to us in Baptism. The font of the church is like a mother's womb, and from it we were born children of God.

The Spirit, Jesus says, is like the wind: you hear it, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes (John 3:8). Nicodemus did not understand at once. But later he defended Jesus, and after the Cross he came openly to bury the Lord. Our new birth also grows slowly, from night into day.

Paul tells us what the new life looks like: put to death what is earthly; get rid of anger, malice, slander and lies; take off the old self and put on the new (Colossians 3:5–10). And in this new family “there is no longer Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave and free; but Christ is all and in all!” (Colossians 3:11).
This week, let us thank God for our Baptism, take off one old habit, and treat every baptised person as a brother or sister in Christ. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, when you were baptised, you were born again as a child of God! The priest poured water and the Holy Spirit came to live in you. The Spirit is like the wind: you cannot see it, but you can see the trees move. When you feel the wind today, say: thank you, Jesus, for my Baptism!

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews repeats a word from the Psalm: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 3:7–8). God does not speak to us about tomorrow. He speaks today.

The people in the wilderness saw great miracles and still hardened their hearts. So the writer says: exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin (Hebrews 3:13). We are responsible for one another's faith.

Jesus says: anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and has passed from death to life (John 5:24). And he promises that the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear his voice and come out (John 5:28–29). When we pray at the graves of our dead, we pray in this hope.

Today we remember St Catherine of Siena. She had little schooling, yet God made her a teacher of the Church. She wrote to the Pope and begged him to return to Rome, and worked for peace and unity. She died at thirty-three, on this day in 1380. She shows us what Jesus said: the Father reveals his secrets to the little ones (Matthew 11:25).
Let us not wait for tomorrow. Today, let us hear his voice, encourage one another, and live as people who have already passed from death to life. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, St Catherine of Siena could not read when she was small, but she loved Jesus with all her heart. Later she wrote letters to the Pope! Jesus says that God shows his secrets to little children. You can know Jesus and love him too, even now!

homily: Dear friends, St Paul came to Corinth, a city that loved fine speeches, and he decided to know nothing among them except Jesus Christ, and him crucified (1 Corinthians 2:2). He came in weakness, fear and much trembling, and yet a Church was born.

Why? Because his preaching was a demonstration of the Spirit and of power, so that their faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God (1 Corinthians 2:4–5). In this Easter season, let us remember: the Risen Lord is the Crucified Lord. He still bears his wounds, now shining with glory.

In the Gospel Jesus says: it is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth (Matthew 15:11). What comes out of the mouth comes from the heart: evil intentions, murder, adultery, theft, false witness, slander (Matthew 15:18–19).
Today many words come out not only through our mouths but through our phones. Before we speak or forward anything about another person, let us ask: is it true, is it kind, is it necessary?
Tomorrow the month of May begins, the month of our Blessed Mother, who kept the words of her Son in her heart. Let us ask her for a clean heart, so that our words may always build up. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says that what makes us bad is not the food we eat, but the bad words that come out of our heart. Tonight, let us ask Jesus for a clean heart, so that only kind words come out of our mouths!

intro: Theme: “Thomas answered him, ‘My Lord and my God!’ Jesus said to him, ‘Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.’”
New Sunday: the peace of the Risen Lord, the Spirit given for the forgiveness of sins, the confession of Mar Thoma, and the community of one heart and soul.

sub: Sent as the Father sent him.
q: For you shall go out in joy, and be led back in peace; the mountains and the hills before you shall burst into song, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands.
Jesus said to them again, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I send you.”
points.apply: Name the fear that locks the door of your heart, and let the Risen Lord come through it with his peace.

q: let the wicked forsake their way, and the unrighteous their thoughts; let them return to the LORD, that he may have mercy on them, and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.
When he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain the sins of any, they are retained.”
points.apply: Go to the Sacrament of Reconciliation during this Easter season.

q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Now the whole group of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one claimed private ownership of any possessions, but everything they owned was held in common.
points.apply: Keep a modern pidiyari: set aside something small each day this season for the poor.

q: See, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands; your walls are continually before me.
Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!” Jesus said to him, “Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.”
points.apply: At every elevation this season, say in your heart the words of Mar Thoma.

concl: On the eighth day the Risen Lord comes through our locked doors, shows us his wounds, breathes his Spirit and forgives our sins.
With Mar Thoma our father in faith we confess him, My Lord and my God, and we live as one heart and soul.
2027-04-04.resolve: This Easter season, go to confession, whisper ‘My Lord and my God’ at every elevation, and keep a daily pidiyari for the poor.

intro: Theme: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
A house of prayer for all peoples, the wisdom of Gamaliel and the joy of the apostles, every spiritual blessing in Christ, and the answer to Thomas's question.

points.h: A house of prayer for all peoples
sub: The foreigner and the dry tree.
The Ethiopian reading Isaiah, and India reached by Thomas.
q: these I will bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God,
points.apply: Welcome one newcomer or lonely person at church this week.

sub: Rejoicing to suffer for the name.
q: Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
because if this plan or this undertaking is of human origin, it will fail; but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them
points.apply: Hand one fear about the Church or your family over to God in prayer.

sub: Chosen before the foundation of the world.
Sealed with the Spirit, the pledge of our inheritance.
q: I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
In him you also, when you had heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and had believed in him, were marked with the seal of the promised Holy Spirit;
points.apply: Begin each day this week by blessing the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

sub: Do not let your hearts be troubled.
Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.
q: You show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy; in your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
points.apply: Bring one honest question about your faith to Jesus in prayer this week.

concl: The Risen Lord gathers all peoples into his Father's house, seals them with his Spirit, and is himself the way home.
Our father Saint Thomas asked the way and followed it to India; let us follow it too.
2027-04-11.resolve: This week, welcome a stranger at church, bless the Father each morning, and pray daily in the name of Jesus for one intention.

intro: Theme: “So you have pain now; but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.”
The God who cannot forget us, the gift that cannot be bought, the mercy that makes the dead alive, and the sorrow that turns into joy.

q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: When you feel forgotten this week, look at your palm and pray: my name is written on your hands.

points.h: The gift that cannot be bought
q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain God's gift with money!
points.apply: Let go of any way you use holy things for honour or advantage.

sub: Seated with him in the heavenly places.
q: Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live.
But God, who is rich in mercy, out of the great love with which he loved us even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ
points.apply: Thank God today for one way he has raised you from a kind of death.

points.h: Your pain will turn into joy
sub: The woman in labour and the Mother at the Cross.
A joy no one can take.
q: Weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning.
So you have pain now; but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
points.apply: Pray every day this week for vocations, and bring one sorrow to the Lord to be turned into joy.

concl: God never forgets his people; he gives his Spirit freely, raises the dead to life, and turns our sorrow into the joy of Easter.
On this day of prayer for vocations, we ask the Lord of the harvest for labourers who will give freely what they have freely received.
2027-04-18.resolve: This week pray daily for a vocation from your family or parish, thank a priest or sister who serves you, and give one sorrow to the Risen Lord.

intro: Theme: “Jesus said to them, ‘Come and have breakfast.’ Now none of the disciples dared to ask him, ‘Who are you?’ because they knew it was the Lord.”
On the Sunday of Mar Addai: the despised Servant exalted, Saul called out of darkness, the new and living way opened to us, and the Risen Lord who prepares the meal.

sub: The day of salvation is now.
q: Sing for joy, O heavens, and exult, O earth; break forth, O mountains, into singing! For the LORD has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his suffering ones.
For he says, “At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you.” See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Sing one Easter hymn of thanksgiving at home this week.

points.h: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
sub: The Lord one with his Church.
q: Now the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
He asked, “Who are you, Lord?” The reply came, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.”
points.apply: Pray this week for those who persecute Christians, that they may meet the Risen Lord.

points.h: Let us approach with a true heart
sub: The new and living way through his flesh.
q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts,
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
points.apply: Invite someone who has stopped coming to the Sunday Qurbana to come with you.

sub: The fire, the fish and the bread.
q: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Jesus said to them, “Come and have breakfast.” Now none of the disciples dared to ask him, “Who are you?” because they knew it was the Lord.
points.apply: At the offertory next Sunday, offer the work of your week to the Lord.

concl: The Lord who called Saul and fed the fishermen calls and feeds us in every Qurbana, prayed in the ancient words of Mar Addai and Mar Mari.
Let us recognise him, come near with a true heart, and bring others to his table.
2027-04-25.resolve: This week, pray for persecutors and the persecuted, offer your work at the altar, and bring one person back to the Sunday assembly.

intro: Theme: “You received without payment; give without payment.”
The barren one who sings, the seven who serve, the record nailed to the Cross, and the Twelve sent out with empty bags.

points.h: My steadfast love shall not depart
sub: A brief moment, an everlasting love.
q: For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love shall not depart from you, and my covenant of peace shall not be removed, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.

For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor rulers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
points.apply: Name one dark time you have come through, and thank God that his love did not move.

points.h: Seven men full of the Spirit
q: I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them; and they shall bear the burden of the people along with you so that you will not bear it all by yourself.
Therefore, friends, select from among yourselves seven men of good standing, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint to this task.
points.apply: Find out who in your parish is being overlooked, and go and see them.

q: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people.
when you were buried with him in baptism, you were also raised with him through faith in the power of God, who raised him from the dead.
points.apply: Bring to the Sacrament of Reconciliation the guilt you still carry, and leave it at the Cross.

q: Since there will never cease to be some in need on the earth, I therefore command you, “Open your hand to the poor and needy neighbor in your land.”
You received without payment; give without payment.
points.apply: Do one act of service this week for which you will receive nothing back.

concl: The Risen Lord widens the tent of his Church, erases our debt and sends us out with empty bags and full hands.
What we received without payment we give without payment, and the word of God spreads.
2027-04-01.resolve: This week, visit one widow or widower, pray for the deacons and seminarians of your eparchy, and do one hidden service without payment.

intro: Theme: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.”
The young men in the fire, Stephen with the face of an angel, the witnesses of faith, and the call to fearless witness.

sub: The fourth man in the fire.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.
But they have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, for they did not cling to life even in the face of death.
points.apply: Tell God in prayer today that you will trust him even if he does not give you what you are asking.

q: Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And all who sat in the council looked intently at him, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
points.apply: Spend time with God before a hard conversation, and let him be seen in you.

q: Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you.

Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight and the sin that clings so closely, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us.
points.apply: Ask one saint or martyr to be your companion this Easter season, and learn their story.

q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.
points.apply: Make one small public act of witness today: grace before meals, a word of faith, a sign of the cross.

concl: The martyrs went with Christ through death into life, and he walked with them in the fire.
We are surrounded by their cloud of witnesses; let us not be afraid to acknowledge him.
2027-04-02.resolve: Today, make one act of public witness, pray for a persecuted Church by name, and forgive one person with Stephen's prayer.

intro: Theme: “For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.”
The stone already rolled away, the empty place, the message to Peter, and the hidden life of the baptised.

points.h: Who will roll away the stone?
sub: Walking with spices and a worry.
q: Weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning.
When they looked up, they saw that the stone, which was very large, had already been rolled back.
points.apply: Take one step towards the conversation or confession you have been dreading.

sub: No one struck off the list.
q: Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity and passing over the transgression of the remnant of your possession? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency.
But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you to Galilee; there you will see him, just as he told you.
points.apply: Read Mark 16:7 with your own name after ‘and’, and believe it.

points.h: Seek the things that are above
q: My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
So if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
points.apply: Begin each morning this week by lifting your mind to God before anything else.

q: For he will hide me in his shelter in the day of trouble; he will conceal me under the cover of his tent; he will set me high on a rock.
for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ who is your life is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory.
points.apply: Thank one person whose hidden faithfulness holds your family or parish together.

concl: The stone is rolled away, the tomb is empty, and the Lord calls back even those who failed him.
Our new life is hidden with him now, and will be revealed with him in glory.
2027-04-03.resolve: This week, walk towards one stone you fear, pray the ‘Queen of Heaven’ each day, and lift your mind to God before you open your phone each morning.

intro: Theme: “Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him; and he vanished from their sight.”
A divided parish, a Lord who waits to be invited, the breaking of the bread, and burning hearts that run back to the community.

sub: One Lord crucified, one name in Baptism.
Unity grows from looking at the Cross.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
points.apply: Pray by name this week for someone in your parish with whom you disagree.

sub: The preacher is not the message.
q: Thus says the LORD: Do not let the wise boast in their wisdom, do not let the mighty boast in their might, do not let the wealthy boast in their wealth;
For Christ did not send me to baptize but to proclaim the gospel, and not with eloquent wisdom, so that the cross of Christ might not be emptied of its power.
points.apply: Next time you praise or criticise a preacher, ask instead what the Lord said to you through him.

sub: He walked ahead as if going on.
The Lord waits to be invited.
q: My lord, if I find favor with you, do not pass by your servant.
But they urged him strongly, saying, “Stay with us, because it is almost evening and the day is now nearly over.” So he went in to stay with them.
points.apply: Make ‘Lord, stay with us’ your night prayer this week.

points.h: Known in the breaking of the bread
sub: Back to Jerusalem that same hour.
q: O taste and see that the LORD is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
Then they told what had happened on the road, and how he had been made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
points.apply: Come to one weekday Holy Qurbana this week and receive him with a burning heart.

concl: The Risen Lord heals our divisions by gathering us at one table.
He waits to be invited; let us say every evening: Stay with us.
2027-04-05.resolve: This week, pray ‘Lord, stay with us’ each night, attend one weekday Holy Qurbana, and take one step to mend a division.

intro: Theme: “If you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me.”
The persecutor turned preacher, the apostle carried in a basket, the glory that comes from God, and Christ hidden in the Law and the Prophets.

points.h: He is the Son of God
sub: The persecutor cannot stop speaking the name.
q: I will tell of the decree of the LORD: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.”
and immediately he began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, saying, “He is the Son of God.”
points.apply: Say one good word about Jesus this week to someone who does not expect it from you.

q: We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped.
but I was let down in a basket through a window in the wall, and escaped from his hands.
points.apply: Ask someone to pray for a burden you have been carrying alone.

points.h: The glory that comes from God
sub: Jesus does not accept human glory.
q: for the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
How can you believe when you accept glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the one who alone is God?
points.apply: Do one good deed in secret this week.

sub: Christ hidden in the Old Testament.
The Law and the Prophets read at the Qurbana.
q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
If you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote about me.
points.apply: Read one Old Testament passage this week and ask where Christ is in it.

concl: The Risen Lord turns persecutors into preachers and makes the proud small enough to be carried.
All Scripture speaks of him; let us seek his glory alone.
2027-04-06.resolve: This week, speak of Jesus to one person, do one hidden act of kindness, and read one Old Testament passage looking for Christ.

intro: Theme: “He has done everything well; he even makes the deaf to hear and the mute to speak.”
The freedom Christ has won, faith working through love, the Lord who heals with touch and word, and creation made new.

points.h: For freedom Christ has set us free
sub: Do not take up a yoke again.
q: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery;
For freedom Christ has set us free. Stand firm, therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
points.apply: Bring one enslaving habit to confession this Easter season.

sub: The whole law in one commandment.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything; the only thing that counts is faith working through love.
points.apply: Do one act of love this week for someone who cannot repay you.

sub: Fingers, spittle, a sigh, a look to heaven.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
Then looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.”
points.apply: Before the Gospel at Holy Qurbana, ask the Lord to open your ears.

q: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
They were astounded beyond measure, saying, “He has done everything well; he even makes the deaf to hear and the mute to speak.”
points.apply: Use your tongue today only for praise and for kind words.

concl: The Risen Christ frees us from every yoke and opens our ears and lips.
Faith that loves is the only faith that counts.
2027-04-07.resolve: This week, bring one enslaving habit to confession, do one hidden act of love, and pray Ephphatha before the Gospel.

intro: Theme: “Then Jesus answered her, ‘Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.’”
A life worthy of the Gospel, the privilege of suffering for Christ, one of the shortest prayers in the Bible, and the children's bread for all nations.

q: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
Only, live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ,
points.apply: Change one habit at work or online that does not match the Gospel.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
For he has graciously granted you the privilege not only of believing in Christ, but of suffering for him as well
points.apply: Offer one pain this week, united to Christ's Cross, for someone in need.

sub: An outsider confesses the Son of David.
She kneels and will not go.
q: Incline your ear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
But she came and knelt before him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
points.apply: Pray ‘Lord, help me’ every time anxiety rises this week.

sub: Not crumbs but the whole loaf.
q: Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed instantly.
points.apply: Keep praying daily for one person you have almost given up on.

concl: The Risen Lord turns suffering into grace and silence into deeper faith.
His table is open to every nation; let us come to it with humble, persevering faith.
2027-04-08.resolve: This week, change one habit unworthy of the Gospel, offer one suffering, and pray ‘Lord, help me’ without giving up.

intro: Theme: “For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.”
The folly of the Cross, Christ the power and wisdom of God, the generous sower, and the grain that dies to bear fruit.

sub: A Saviour on a slave's cross.
The wisdom of the world made foolish.
An act of love that saves.
q: so I will again do amazing things with this people, shocking and amazing. The wisdom of their wise shall perish, and the discernment of the discerning shall be hidden.
For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
points.apply: Spend five minutes before a crucifix today and thank the Lord.

points.h: Christ the power and wisdom of God
sub: The flowering Cross of the Resurrection.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
but to those who are the called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross slowly and reverently each time you pray this week.

points.h: A sower went out to sow
sub: The path, the rock, the thorns.
The word that does not return empty.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
“Listen! A sower went out to sow.”
points.apply: Share one Gospel verse with someone this week.

q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy.
Other seed fell into good soil and brought forth grain, growing up and increasing and yielding thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.”
points.apply: Cut back one ‘thorn’ that chokes God's word in you.

concl: The Cross that looked like defeat is the power of God, and its harvest is Easter.
The sower is generous; let us become good soil.
2027-04-09.resolve: This week, pray before the Cross, cut back one thorn, and share one verse of the Gospel.

intro: Theme: “Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself.”
Love above all, the peace of Christ as umpire, a home where the word dwells and songs are sung, and the real body of the Risen Lord.

q: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can floods drown it.
Above all, clothe yourselves with love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony.
points.apply: Forgive one hurt from this week before you sleep tonight.

points.h: Let the peace of Christ rule
q: the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which indeed you were called in the one body. And be thankful.
points.apply: Before a decision this week, ask what keeps Christ's peace in your heart.

sub: Not visiting but living in the house.
q: O sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; teach and admonish one another in all wisdom; and with gratitude in your hearts sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs to God.
points.apply: Keep family evening prayer with a Gospel reading and a hymn every day this week.

q: and after my skin has been thus destroyed, then in my flesh I shall see God,
Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself. Touch me and see; for a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.
points.apply: Pray at the grave of a loved one in hope of the resurrection.

concl: The Risen Lord is no ghost: he lives in his glorified body and gives himself to us as food.
Let love clothe us, his peace rule us, and his word dwell in our homes.
2027-04-10.resolve: This week, keep family evening prayer daily with the Gospel and a hymn, let Christ's peace decide, and do everything in his name with thanks.

intro: Theme: “Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.”
The patience of the farmer, the lamps of the bridesmaids, and the Risen Bridegroom who is coming.

sub: The early and the late rains.
Do not grumble against one another.
q: Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!
You also must be patient. Strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near.
points.apply: Replace one grumble today with a prayer for the person you were about to complain about.

q: I slept, but my heart was awake. Listen! my beloved is knocking.
When the foolish took their lamps, they took no oil with them; but the wise took flasks of oil with their lamps.
points.apply: Choose one daily practice of prayer and keep it faithfully this week.

q: For as a young man marries a young woman, so shall your builder marry you, and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.
But at midnight there was a shout, ‘Look! Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.’
points.apply: Come to the next Qurbana as to a wedding feast, ready and glad.

concl: We wait for the Risen Lord like farmers who keep working and like bridesmaids whose lamps are full.
He is not a stranger but the Bridegroom who loves us; every day may be the day of his knock.
2027-04-12.resolve: This week keep your lamp burning with daily prayer, and turn every grumble into a prayer.

intro: Theme: “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.”
The rule of life of a young church, the Easter life in three lines, and the soil of our hearts.

sub: Encourage the fainthearted, help the weak.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
esteem them very highly in love because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves.
points.apply: Thank one person who serves your parish, by name, this week.

sub: Joy that rests on the Resurrection.
A heart turned to God all day.
q: I will bless the LORD at all times; his praise shall continually be in my mouth.
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
points.apply: Each night this week tell the Lord three things you are thankful for.

sub: The thorns of worry and wealth.
The good soil and the hundredfold.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
And these are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.
points.apply: Name the thorn that chokes your prayer, and hand it to the Lord every morning.

concl: A young church learns to honour its servants, to care for the weak, and to live in joy, prayer and thanksgiving.
The seed of the word is always good; the Risen Lord asks us to become good soil.
2027-04-13.resolve: This week thank one who serves, give thanks each night, and pull out one thorn that chokes the word.

intro: Theme: “For to me, living is Christ and dying is gain.”
A prisoner who no longer fears death, an apostle torn between heaven and his people, and the hand that cleanses the leper.

q: Because your steadfast love is better than life, my lips will praise you.
For to me, living is Christ and dying is gain.
points.apply: Finish the sentence “For me, living is …” honestly, and ask the Lord to make the answer Christ.

sub: To depart and be with Christ.
To remain for your progress and joy.
Love for this life as service.
q: For I know that my Redeemer lives, and that at the last he will stand upon the earth; and after my skin has been thus destroyed, then in my flesh I shall see God,
I am hard pressed between the two: my desire is to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better;
points.apply: Pray this week for someone who is dying, and for a peaceful death for yourself.

sub: Restored to the people of God.
q: He shall remain unclean as long as he has the disease; he is unclean. He shall live alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
He stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I do choose. Be made clean!” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
points.apply: Go to Confession soon, and reach out this week to one person whom others avoid.

concl: Because Christ is risen, death is gain for those whose life is Christ, and this life becomes a time of loving service.
The Risen Lord still stretches out his hand to touch and cleanse, and he sends us to do the same.
2027-04-14.resolve: This week let Christ be your life, bring your hidden wounds to Confession, and touch someone who is shut out.

intro: Theme: “He woke up and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, ‘Peace! Be still!’ Then the wind ceased, and there was a dead calm.”
The joyful generosity of the poor, the great exchange of Christ, and the Lord who calms the storm.

sub: They gave themselves first to the Lord.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
for during a severe ordeal of affliction, their abundant joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in a wealth of generosity on their part.
points.apply: Set aside a small daily gift for the poor this week.

sub: The generous act of our Lord.
The poverty of the manger and the tomb.
q: He raises the poor from the dust, and lifts the needy from the ash heap,
For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
points.apply: Complete one good work of charity that you began and left unfinished.

q: he made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
He woke up and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” Then the wind ceased, and there was a dead calm.
points.apply: When fear rises today, pray slowly: Jesus, you are in my boat.

concl: The poor Macedonians teach us that generosity flows from first giving ourselves to the Lord who became poor for us.
The Risen Christ is in the boat of the Church; fear closes our hands, but faith opens them.
2027-04-15.resolve: This week give a daily handful to the poor, finish one unfinished good work, and meet every storm with faith.

intro: Theme: “After looking around at all of them, he said to him, ‘Stretch out your hand.’ He did so, and his hand was restored.”
Bearing with the weak as Christ bore our insults, praising God with one voice, and doing good on the Lord's Day.

sub: The insults that fell on Christ.
q: a bruised reed he will not break, and a dimly burning wick he will not quench; he will faithfully bring forth justice.
We who are strong ought to put up with the failings of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
points.apply: Be patient all week with one person whose weakness irritates you.

q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
May the God of steadfastness and encouragement grant you to live in harmony with one another, in accordance with Christ Jesus,
points.apply: Take the first step toward someone with whom you disagree.

sub: To do good or to do harm.
The Lord's Day and the works of God.
q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to destroy it?”
points.apply: Next Sunday, after the Qurbana, do one work of mercy.

concl: Christ did not please himself; he carried our insults and healed the withered hand.
His disciples bear with the weak, seek harmony, and keep the Lord's Day with works of love.
2027-04-16.resolve: This week bear with one weak brother or sister, pray for the unity of the Church, and plan a work of mercy for Sunday.

intro: Theme: “Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell you?”
Faith that is alive in works, the Lord who must be obeyed, and the house built on rock.

q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
So faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.
points.apply: Do one concrete act of help this week, not only a promise to pray.

q: They come to you as people come, and they sit before you as my people, and they hear your words, but they will not obey them.
Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell you?
points.apply: Choose one teaching of Jesus you know but do not practise, and begin today.

q: The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, my God, my rock in whom I take refuge,
That one is like a man building a house, who dug deeply and laid the foundation on rock; when a flood arose, the river burst against that house but could not shake it, because it had been well built.
points.apply: Ask the Blessed Virgin Mary each day this week to help you hear the word and do it.

concl: Living faith shows itself in love, as a living tree shows itself in fruit.
Those who hear the Risen Lord and act on his word build on the rock that no flood can shake.
2027-04-17.resolve: This week feed or help one person in need, put one forgotten teaching of Jesus into practice, and pray with Mary to be a doer of the word.

intro: Theme: “Then the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’”
The good confession before Pilate, the King who dwells in unapproachable light, the beloved Son sent to the vineyard, and the rejected stone made cornerstone.

sub: Two witnesses called into the room.
Our confession at the font and in the Creed.
q: You are my witnesses, says the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he.
In the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who in his testimony before Pontius Pilate made the good confession, I charge you
points.apply: Say the Creed slowly once today as your own confession of faith.

sub: The hidden God made near in the Risen Christ.
Holy fear and holy nearness at the altar.
q: You are clothed with honor and majesty, wrapped in light as with a garment.
It is he alone who has immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or can see; to him be honor and eternal dominion. Amen.
points.apply: Make a slow, reverent bow before the altar the next time you enter the church.

points.h: I will send my beloved son
sub: The Son thrown out of the vineyard.
Easter: the rejected stone becomes the cornerstone.
q: The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone.
Then the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.’
points.apply: Choose one fruit to give God this week: prayer, mercy or a gift to the poor.

concl: The Son whom the tenants rejected is risen, and the vineyard is now in our hands.
Let us keep our confession clean and give the Owner his fruit.
2027-04-19.resolve: This week, renew your baptismal confession in the Creed, speak the truth gently when it costs you, and give God one clear fruit of mercy.

intro: Theme: “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.”
Hope not in uncertain riches, the deposit of faith guarded and handed on, and the God who does the impossible.

points.h: Not on the uncertainty of riches
sub: The life that really is life.
q: Put no confidence in extortion, and set no vain hopes on robbery; if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.

As for those who in the present age are rich, command them not to be haughty, or to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but rather on God who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment.
points.apply: Give something away today before you buy anything for yourself.

points.h: Guard what has been entrusted to you
sub: False knowledge and the plain faith.
Kept by living and handing on.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the LORD?
Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Avoid the profane chatter and contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge;
points.apply: Teach a child one prayer or one line of the Creed this week.

points.h: For God all things are possible
sub: A hundredfold and the renewal of all things.
q: For I am about to create new heavens and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered or come to mind.
But Jesus looked at them and said, “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.”
points.apply: Bring to God one situation you have given up on, and leave it with him.

concl: The God who raised his Son from the tomb can release a heart tied to its possessions.
Let us hope in him, give generously and guard the faith we have received.
2027-04-20.resolve: This week, give before you buy, hand on one piece of the faith to a child, and ask God for the impossible.

intro: Theme: “Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.”
The king-priest with bread and wine, the Risen Priest who always intercedes, and the witnesses to the Son.

points.h: King of righteousness, king of peace
sub: Bread and wine, blessing and tithe.
A living picture of the eternal Son.
q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.
Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
points.apply: Pray today for the priest who baptised you.

points.h: One of whom it is testified that he lives
sub: Mortal priests and the Living One.
A priesthood that never passes on.
q: The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”

but he holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever. Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: When you cannot find words, ask Jesus to pray for you, and rest in his prayer.

q: Only on the evidence of two or three witnesses shall a charge be sustained.
But I have a testimony greater than John’s. The works that the Father has given me to complete, the very works that I am doing, testify on my behalf that the Father has sent me.
points.apply: Do one good work this week that points to Christ rather than to yourself.

concl: The eternal Priest lives and intercedes for us, and offers himself on our altars.
Let us thank God for our priests and become witnesses whose works speak of Christ.
2027-04-21.resolve: This week, pray for priests by name, give God the first part of each day, and let one work of yours bear witness to Christ.

intro: Theme: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.”
False teachers who deny the Master who bought them, the apostolic faith as our test, and worship that reaches the heart.

points.h: They will deny the Master who bought them
q: Thus says the LORD of hosts: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you; they are deluding you. They speak visions of their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.

But false prophets also arose among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you, who will secretly bring in destructive opinions. They will even deny the Master who bought them—bringing swift destruction on themselves.
points.apply: Before you share a religious message, ask whether it leads to Christ and his Church.

points.h: Hold fast to the apostolic faith
sub: The commandment spoken through the apostles.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
So then, brothers and sisters, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you were taught by us, either by word of mouth or by our letter.
points.apply: Teach or review one article of the Creed at home this week.

sub: Not against tradition, but against avoiding love.
A new heart that honours father and mother.
q: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is a human commandment learned by rote;
For one believes with the heart and so is justified, and one confesses with the mouth and so is saved.
points.apply: Do one concrete act of care for your parents or an elderly relative today.

concl: The Lord who bought us with his Blood wants our faith whole and our hearts near.
Let us hold to what the apostles handed down and let our love begin at home.
2027-04-22.resolve: This week, test the voices you follow, remember the price of your redemption before a crucifix, and honour your parents with a deed of love.

intro: Theme: “Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”
The baptismal light of the Risen Christ, the Spirit-filled life of song and thanksgiving, and the loaves taken, blessed, broken and given.

sub: A hymn of the newly baptised.
The light that shows and heals.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
Therefore it says, “Sleeper, awake! Rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”
points.apply: Begin tomorrow with the prayer: Christ, shine on me today.

sub: Making the most of the time.
Not drunk with wine, but filled with the Spirit.
Singing and giving thanks for everything.
q: O sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth. Sing to the LORD, bless his name; tell of his salvation from day to day.

as you sing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs among yourselves, singing and making melody to the Lord in your hearts, giving thanks to God the Father at all times and for everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Sing one hymn together at family prayer this week.

points.h: You give them something to eat
q: So he repeated, “Give it to the people and let them eat, for thus says the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have some left.’”
Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, and blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people; and he divided the two fish among them all.
points.apply: Offer a skill, some time or a little money to those who feed the hungry.

concl: The Risen Christ shines on us, fills us with his Spirit and feeds us with his Body.
Let us wake, give thanks and bring our small loaves to him.
2027-04-23.resolve: This week, pray each morning for Christ's light, give thanks before every meal, and share bread with someone who is hungry.

intro: Theme: “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.”
On the feast of Mar Geevarghese Sahada: the God who shut the lions' mouths, the Church that prayed for Peter, power made perfect in weakness, and life found by losing it for Christ.

points.h: The God who shut the lions' mouths
sub: Daniel prays three times a day.
The sealed stone and the long night.
Found alive at dawn, because he trusted.
q: My God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths so that they would not hurt me, because I was found blameless before him; and also before you, O king, I have done no wrong.
who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
points.apply: Keep three short moments of prayer today, whatever happens.

q: The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.
While Peter was kept in prison, the church prayed fervently to God for him.
points.apply: Pray a decade of the rosary for persecuted Christians.

sub: When I am weak, then I am strong.
q: He gives power to the faint, and strengthens the powerless.
but he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” So, I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
points.apply: Offer one weakness to Christ today and ask his power to dwell there.

points.h: Lose your life to find it
sub: Not even a cup of cold water forgotten.
q: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will ever touch them.
Those who find their life will lose it, and those who lose their life for my sake will find it.
points.apply: Do one hidden kindness today for someone who cannot repay you.

concl: St George chose Christ above everything and found his life in the Risen Lord.
Let us ask his prayers to be strong in weakness and faithful in small things.
2027-04-24.resolve: This week, pray daily for persecuted Christians, offer your weaknesses to Christ, and lose a little of your life for him in hidden service.

intro: Theme: “For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.”
The sign of Jonah fulfilled in the Resurrection, the repentance of Nineveh, and the fiery ordeal borne with joy in the name of Christ.

points.h: No sign but the sign of Jonah
sub: A generation that asks for proof.
The sign already given: the empty tomb.
q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Make a simple act of faith in the Risen Lord today, without asking for any further sign.

sub: The queen who travelled to listen.
The One greater than Jonah and Solomon.
q: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity that he had said he would bring upon them; and he did not do it.
The people of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and see, something greater than Jonah is here!
points.apply: Choose one thing to change this week because the Risen Lord has spoken to you.

points.h: Glorify God because you bear this name
sub: Do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal.
Sharing Christ's sufferings, sharing his joy.
Entrust yourself and keep doing good.
q: See, I have refined you, but not like silver; I have tested you in the furnace of adversity.
Yet if any of you suffers as a Christian, do not consider it a disgrace, but glorify God because you bear this name.
points.apply: Make the sign of the Cross openly before a meal, and pray each day this week for persecuted Christians.

concl: The Risen Christ is the one sign given to our generation, greater than Jonah and greater than Solomon.
Let us repent like Nineveh and bear his name with joy, even in the fire.
2027-04-26.resolve: This week, make an act of faith without conditions, change one thing at the Lord's word, and pray daily for those who suffer as Christians.

intro: Theme: “But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.”
The mirror of the word, the religion of the bridled tongue and the open hand, and the fig tree that had only leaves.

sub: The mirror that shows our true face.
q: To them you are like a singer of love songs, one who has a beautiful voice and plays well on an instrument; they hear what you say, but they will not do it.
For if any are hearers of the word and not doers, they are like those who look at themselves in a mirror;
points.apply: Write down one sentence from Sunday's Gospel and put it into practice before next Sunday.

sub: Orphans and widows in their distress.
q: learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.
Religion that is pure and undefiled before God, the Father, is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
points.apply: Visit or telephone one widow or elderly person living alone this week.

sub: A tree that promises and does not give.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
Whatever you ask for in prayer with faith, you will receive.
points.apply: Pray each day this week, with faith, for one fruit of love you want the Lord to grow in you.

concl: The word is a mirror, true religion is mercy and purity, and the Lord looks for fruit.
The Risen Lord gives the grace; let us bear the fruit.
2027-04-27.resolve: This week, do one word of the Gospel, visit one person who is alone, and pray with faith for the fruit of love.

intro: Theme: “Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.”
Nicodemus by night, the wind of the Spirit, the new birth of Baptism, and the new self in whom Christ is all and in all.

sub: A teacher who comes by night.
Can one who has grown old be born again?
q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
Jesus answered him, “Very truly, I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God without being born from above.”
points.apply: Find the date of your Baptism and thank God for it this week.

points.h: The wind blows where it chooses
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
The wind blows where it chooses, and you hear the sound of it, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit.
points.apply: Each morning this week, pray: Come, Holy Spirit, blow where you choose in my life today.

sub: Christ is all and in all.
q: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
As many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
points.apply: Choose one sin of the mouth to fight for the rest of the Easter season, and treat one person you look down on as a brother or sister.

concl: We were born from above in Baptism, and the Spirit still blows where he chooses.
Let us take off the old self and wear Christ, in whom there are no walls between us.
2027-04-28.resolve: This week, thank God for your Baptism, pray daily to the Holy Spirit, and fight one sin of the mouth.

intro: Theme: “Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.”
The ‘today’ of God's voice, the life that begins now and the voice that will open every grave, and St Catherine of Siena, to whom the Father revealed his secrets.

points.h: Today, if you hear his voice
sub: The hard hearts of the wilderness.
q: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice!
But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called “today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
points.apply: Do today the good thing you have been putting off, and encourage one person in faith.

sub: The hour that is now here.
The hour when the graves will open.
q: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
Very truly, I tell you, the hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
points.apply: Pray this week for your dead by name, professing faith in the resurrection of the body.

sub: A daughter of an ordinary family in Siena.
Truth spoken in love to the powerful.
q: Come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
If we confess our sins, he who is faithful and just will forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Pentecost, and pray for the Pope and the unity of the Church.

concl: God speaks today, gives eternal life now, and will raise the dead at the last day.
St Catherine shows that whoever listens like a child can set the world on fire.
2027-04-29.resolve: This week, act on God's word without delay, pray for your dead, and make a good confession through the prayers of St Catherine.

intro: Theme: “For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.”
The Crucified preached in weakness, the heart from which words come, and the clean heart of the Mother of God at the threshold of her month.

sub: A trembling preacher in a proud city.
The power of God in weakness.
The Risen One keeps his wounds.
q: Thus says the LORD: Do not let the wise boast in their wisdom, do not let the mighty boast in their might, do not let the wealthy boast in their wealth;
so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God.
points.apply: Pray before a crucifix for five minutes today, thanking the Risen Lord for his wounds.

sub: From the hands to the heart.
The list that begins with thoughts.
q: Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.
But what comes out of the mouth proceeds from the heart, and this is what defiles.
points.apply: Examine your words of this week, spoken and typed, and confess any false witness or slander.

points.h: Create in me a clean heart
sub: Words that come out through the fingers.
The Mother who kept all in her heart.
q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
points.apply: Pray the Marian month devotion with your family from tomorrow, asking for clean hearts.

concl: The Crucified and Risen Lord is the power of God, and he looks at the heart.
Let us keep our hearts clean, so that our words may build up, with the help of our Blessed Mother.
2027-04-30.resolve: This week, pray before the crucifix, check every message before forwarding it, and begin the Marian month with your family.
